title: Introduction
description: Spools is an open source CRM framework. It gives your coding agents the sign-in, data layer, security, search, email and tests, so they only write what is specific to your business. A CRM built with it is called a Spool.
text: Introduction Spools is an open source CRM framework. It gives your coding agents the sign-in, data layer, security, search, email and tests, so they only write what is specific to your business. A CRM built with it is called a Spool. A Spool is a config, your services and your own code, put together in one file: What you get Pages for your objects. Spreadsheet tables with inline editing, drag-and-drop boards, record pages with a timeline, forms, reports, and CSV import and export. Search and filters. Cmd+K finds records, notes, emails, calls, tasks, and files. Every list filters by any field, through relations, and by activity. Email. Sequences that keep their place in your database, one-off email from a teammate's own mailbox, and a timeline of the mail and meetings they have with contacts. Marketing. The tracking tags your website carries and the code for the ones it is missing, social posts that a teammate approves before they go out, and ad results. Agents and workflows. A Swirls assistant that reads and updates records, and workflows that run when a record changes or someone presses a button. Your own code. Hooks, handlers, pages, endpoints, and services. Where to start If you want to Read Build one with your agent Build with coding agents See one running Quickstart Decide whether it suits you When to use Spools Describe your business Configuration Choose sign-in, a database, and the rest Adapters Add behavior of your own Extending Put it in production Deployment Understand how it works Architecture Where it stands Spools is in its 0.x releases. It works end to end, and minor versions may include breaking changes, which the changelog explains. The status table says what has been tested and how, and the roadmap says what is next.

title: Quickstart
description: Make a CRM, add a field and a board, and create a task when a deal is won. You need Bun 1.4 or newer and no accounts.
text: Quickstart Make a CRM, add a field and a board, and create a task when a deal is won. You need Bun 1.4 or newer and no accounts. Make a Spool Open http://localhost:3000. You are signed in, and there are companies, contacts, and deals to look at. Records are in a Postgres inside the server, which keeps its data in.data/pglite. The development sign-in lets you straight in. A production build refuses to start with it. Look around File What it holds crm.config.json Objects, fields, views, actions, automations, and email sequences src/spool.server.ts The services your CRM runs on src/app/extensions.ts Your hooks and handlers src/routes One small file per page. Delete one to drop a page, or write your own swirls Swirls workflows and the assistant Add a field Contacts have no field for LinkedIn. Add one under objects.contacts.fields in crm.config.json: Check the config and regenerate what is made from it, then restart the server: Open a contact. The field is on the page and in the form, it can be added as a column, and Cmd+K finds people by it. Add a board Views are part of an object. Add one to objects.companies.views that groups companies by industry: Run bun run crm:gen and restart. The view menu on Companies now offers By industry, and dragging a card to another column changes the company's industry. React to a change Hooks run for every change, whoever makes it: a teammate, a CSV import, or the assistant. This one makes a task when a deal is won. Add hooks to what is already in src/app/extensions.ts: Drag a deal to Won and open Tasks. Choose real services Each service is one line in src/spool.server.ts. To keep records in your own Postgres and let people sign in with Clerk: Install what they use and set their variables in.env: The server says at startup which services are on and what the others still need. Create the tables with bun run db:push. Next Say who may sign in with access. Read about signing in, databases, and writing an adapter. Add workflows and the assistant. Deploy it.

title: Build with coding agents
description: Open your Spool in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or another coding agent and say what you need. This page covers what the agent edits and what checks its work.
text: Build with coding agents Open your Spool in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or another coding agent and say what you need. This page covers what the agent edits and what checks its work. Start Paste this into your agent. It asks about your business, makes the Spool and builds your CRM in it: The page it reads is plain text, so you can see what your agent is told before you paste. Or make the Spool yourself: Then open the folder in your agent and ask: Build our CRM. We sell commercial insurance, and we track companies, the people at them, policies with a renewal date, and claims. Policies move from quoted to bound to renewed or lost. Email the account manager 60 days before a policy renews. Every new Spool has an AGENTS.md that tells the agent where each kind of change goes, and a CLAUDE.md that points to it. What an agent edits Most changes are a few lines in one of these places. The request Where it goes Track something, show it, or move it along crm.config.json: objects, fields, pipelines, views Email people on a schedule campaigns in crm.config.json When something happens, do something automations in the config, or a hook in src/app/extensions.ts A page or an endpoint nobody else needs A file in src/routes Use a different sign-in, database, or service src/spool.server.ts The framework is a package, so your agent never edits it and you never merge it. What checks the agent's work Ask the agent to run bun run check before it is done. Each of these stops with a message that says what to change. The config. Every key it knows is checked against a schema: a column for a field that doesn't exist, a board grouped by something that isn't a select, an action that runs nothing. A key the schema doesn't know is ignored, so a misspelt one does nothing. crm.config.schema.json gives the agent the same checks as it types. Who is asking. Lint refuses a server function or an endpoint that doesn't check the session first ( handlers). Types. Records, hooks and routes are typed from the config and the route tree. The browser bundle. bun run build fails if Effect, which server code runs on, reached it. The keys. A production server refuses to start without the keys for its sign-in and database, or with the development sign-in on. Spools comes with one access check for every request, row-level security on every table, tokens sealed before they are stored, and a time limit on every read from an outside service. Read Architecture and Security for how. What to ask for "Add a renewals pipeline with a board by status, and a saved view of what is due this quarter." "When a deal is won, create a project from it and give its owner a task to send the welcome pack." "Email new leads on day 0, day 3, and day 10. Stop when they become a customer." "Import this CSV of our contacts. Keep the owner and the last contacted date." "Add a page that shows stock levels from our warehouse API next to the open orders." "Use Better Auth instead of Clerk, and keep files in our S3 bucket." Moving from another CRM Export your companies, contacts, and deals as CSV from HubSpot, Salesforce, a spreadsheet, or wherever they are now. Describe the fields you use in crm.config.json, then import each file from the list page: columns are matched to fields by key or label, and relations by the related record's title. An import is limited to 1,000 rows and does not fire automations, so split large files, or ask your agent for a script that uses createRecord.

title: When to use Spools
description: Spools is for teams that want a CRM shaped around their work and build software with coding agents or TypeScript.

sections.title: What you need to run one

text: When to use Spools Spools is for teams that want a CRM shaped around their work and build software with coding agents or TypeScript. Choose Spools when You want your agents to build it. They write the part that is yours, on sign-in, data, security and email that are already built. Your objects aren't the usual ones. You track jobs, sites, policies, or placements, and you want them to be first-class records with their own pipelines. You want the data in your own database. Records are ordinary tables in your Postgres, which your other software can read. The CRM has to do something particular. Winning a deal should open a project, or a new contact should be checked against another system. Hooks and handlers are plain TypeScript in your repository. You have already chosen your services. You use a certain sign-in provider, mail provider, or cloud, and the CRM should use them too. You want agents working on records. The assistant and your Swirls workflows go through the same checks, hooks, and timeline as your team. You build CRMs for clients. Each client's CRM is a small repository: a config, a file of services, and whatever is theirs alone. The framework updates as a package. Choose something else when Nobody on the team works with code or coding agents. Views, filters, and reports can be changed in the app, while objects, fields, and services are changed in files. A hosted CRM is a better fit. You need a marketplace of plugins today. Spools has extension points and a handful of adapters. It does not have a catalog of third-party apps. You need a telephone dialer, quoting, or billing. None of these is built in. You need permissions per record or per field. Everyone who may use a Spool can see and change every record. The access list decides who that is. You need a stable API today. Spools is in its 0.x releases, and minor versions may include breaking changes. What you need to run one Runtime Bun 1.4 or newer, in a container or on a VM Database Postgres 15 or newer (tested on 17) Sign-in Clerk, or Better Auth in your own database Optional A mail provider, a place for files, a key for the vault, a Swirls project Spools is written with TanStack Start and Effect. You can configure a Spool and write hooks and pages without knowing either. You need Effect to write an adapter or to work on the framework. Compared with a template Spools began as a template you copied and merged updates into. The framework is now a package. Your repository holds your own files and a version number, so you never merge the framework.

title: Configuration reference
description: The CRM is defined by crm.config.json at the top of your app's folder. The full contract is packages/spools/src/crm/config-schema.ts; crm.config.schema.json is generated from it so your editor can autocomplete and validate the file.
text: Configuration reference The CRM is defined by crm.config.json at the top of your app's folder. The full contract is packages/spools/src/crm/config-schema.ts; crm.config.schema.json is generated from it so your editor can autocomplete and validate the file. After any change: crm:gen stops with a precise error (path and message) when the config is invalid. Top level Key Required Description version yes Config format version. Currently 1. app.name yes Your business name. Shown in the CRM, as " CRM" in the browser tab, and on the sign-in and unsubscribe pages. app.timezone no Where the business keeps its calendar, as an IANA name such as "America/New_York" (default "UTC"). Decides when "today" and "this month" begin in filters. access yes Who may use the CRM. See Access. objects yes The record types. See Objects. files no The shared library on the Files page: { "label": "Company files", "folders": ["Templates"] }. The library exists without it. See Files. automations no Run something when records change. See Automations. app.sendingHours no The hours a sequence's later emails may go out in, on the clock of app.timezone: { "from": "08:00", "to": "18:00" }, weekdays only unless "weekdaysOnly": false. See Campaigns. campaigns no Durable email sequences. See Campaigns. guides no Replace, turn off or add the short guides that show people around. See Guides. assistant no How the Ask page presents the assistant. See The assistant's page. Access The CRM is deny-by-default. A user must be signed in and have a verified primary email that matches the allowlist. At least one entry is required. With Clerk, restrict sign-ups there too (Clerk dashboard → Restrictions) so strangers can't create accounts at all. Objects Each key under objects is an object key (camelCase, used in URLs and the database). companies becomes the Company model and the companies table. Key Required Description label, labelPlural yes Display names. icon no Sidebar icon: users, user, building, handshake, briefcase, calendar, checklist, clipboard, check, ticket, home, file, box. titleField yes Field used as the record's name everywhere. model no Override the Prisma model name (default: PascalCase singular of the key). fields yes See Fields. views yes At least one. See Views. actions no Buttons on the record page. See Actions. files no Give each of this object's records a folder in the file store and a Files tab. { "folders": ["Drawings", "Proposal"] } names folders made inside each record's folder; "under": "<relation field>" nests a record's folder inside the related record's. See Files. Reserved object keys: assistant, settings, new, tasks, notes, reports, workflows, integrations, files, api, crm, unsubscribe. Every object also gets system fields id, createdAt, updatedAt and createdBy, which you can use in views but not redefine. Fields Common options for every field: Key Description type One of the types below. label Display label (default: the key in Title Case). description Help text under the input. required Not-null column and a required input. searchable Found by search: Cmd+K, the box on every list, and relation pickers. Text-like fields only. The title field is always searched. encrypted Field-level encryption intent. See Encryption. Type Stored as Extra options text, longtext, email, phone, url text default (string) number double precision default (number) currency numeric(14,2) currency (ISO code, default USD), default boolean boolean default date date datetime timestamptz select text options: [{ value, label?, color?, probability?, when? }], default, dependsOn. See Pipelines and stages relation <key>_id foreign key to: target object key user text A person on your team (owner, assignee). Shown as a picker of everyone on the access allowlist; stores the auth provider's id for them Need a type that isn't here? Add one in two files. Colors: gray, red, orange, amber, green, teal, blue, indigo, purple, pink. Relations are many-to-one. Optional relations are cleared when the target is deleted; required relations block the delete. When writing a relation through the API or the assistant, pass <field>Id (for example companyId). In the app a relation is chosen by searching the related object, in forms, in a table cell and in a filter. The search looks at the related object's title and its searchable fields, so a contact can be found by email as well as by name. Every word typed must be found in one of them. It works the same for ten records or ten thousand. Select values are stored as plain text, so adding options never needs a migration. Removing an option leaves existing records with that value. Pipelines and stages A stage is a select field. Two option keys turn it into a sales pipeline: probability (0 to 100) is the chance of winning a record at that stage. When any option has one, boards show a weighted total beside each column's sum, and Reports adds a weighted total to the field's breakdown. when limits an option to some values of another select, named by the field's dependsOn. That gives one object several pipelines, each with its own stages. Options without when belong to every pipeline. Forms and pickers only offer the stages that apply, and the server rejects any other value whoever sends it (the CRM, a CSV import, the assistant). Moving a record to another pipeline moves it to that pipeline's first stage, unless its stage belongs to both. A new record takes the stage's default if it applies to the chosen pipeline, and the pipeline's first stage if not. dependsOn must name a select on the same object that doesn't depend on a field itself. Give each pipeline its own board with a view filter: Encryption "encrypted": "storage" | "eq" | "match" | "search" marks a field for CipherStash searchable encryption: Mode Queries on ciphertext storage none (encrypted at rest only) eq exact match match free-text search search exact match, range and free-text The mode also decides what the app will ask of the field today: which filter operators it offers, and whether search reads it. An encrypted field's values are never part of the index the browser searches, apart from a record's title. Status: @cipherstash/stack-prisma doesn't support Prisma 8 yet, so marked fields are currently stored as plaintext. crm:gen prints a warning for each one. Keep the markers: once support lands, the generator will emit encrypted column types and no config change will be needed. Views table: a spreadsheet. columns are field keys (including system columns: createdAt, updatedAt, createdBy, and the activity dates lastActivityAt, lastContactedAt and nextTaskDue), with an optional default sort: one { "field", "dir" }, or a list of up to three. Cells edit in place; column headers sort and filter; rows can be selected and deleted in bulk. A relation sorts by the related record's title. board: a kanban grouped by a select field; each option becomes a column. Drag a card to another column to change the field. Columns show a count, and a total of the first currency field in cardFields. filters (either type) starts the view showing only the records that match. The short form pins fields to a value: { "pipeline": "sales" } or { "active": true }. The long form is a list of conditions with operators, such as [{ "field": "value", "op": "gte", "value": 5000 }]; every field type has its own operators, and conditions can reach through relations. See Search and filters. A board filtered to one value of the field its groupBy depends on only shows the columns that apply, and a record created from a filtered view starts out matching it. The first view is the default; the rest are in the view menu ( ?view=<id>). Tables show 50 records a page; boards show up to 500 cards. Every list can be searched, filtered by any field and sorted by up to three columns: see Search and filters. Views saved in the app The views in the config are the starting point. In the CRM, anyone can change a view's columns, sort, filters and footer calculations (sum, average, min, max, filled, empty), or create a new view from the view menu. Those changes are stored in the saved_views table and shared with everyone, so they need no deploy. Columns and calculations are saved as they are changed. Filters and sort are tried first: they go in the page address, so the list can be linked to, and are written to the view when someone presses Save. "Save as a new view" makes a view for everyone or one only its maker sees. Changing a config view stores an override. "Reset to default" in the view menu deletes it and the view goes back to what the config says. Views created in the app can be renamed and deleted there. If you later remove a field from the config, saved views drop it. A config change can't break a saved view. Built into every CRM These need no configuration: Page What it does Home Record counts, your open tasks, recent activity, and a box that asks the assistant Tasks To-dos with a due date and assignee, optionally linked to a record Files A file browser over the whole drive: a folder per record, a shared library, and any folders the team adds. Needs a file store: see Files Notes Titled notes, optionally linked to a record Reports Team activity: calls, emails, meetings, completed tasks and notes per teammate for a period you pick, with CSV export. Records created per week, and a breakdown of every select field. If the object has a currency field, each breakdown also totals it, weighted by win probability when the options have one. Workflows Your automations, record actions and campaigns, with recent runs Ask The assistant, laid out like the chat assistants people already use: past chats in the sidebar, a reply column, and a box at the bottom. Needs Swirls: see The assistant Every page also has a short guide, offered to each person once and replayable from Help at the bottom of the sidebar. Record pages add an activity timeline, favourites, and (for objects with an email field) a button that sends a one-off email, from the teammate's own mailbox when their sign-in allows it and otherwise through your email provider. Calls and meetings are logged from a record page with an outcome, when they took place and notes. Team activity report Reports opens with a table of what each teammate did in a period (today, this or last week or month, the last 30 or 90 days, this year, or a custom range of up to two years): Column Counts Calls Calls logged on a record, with how many connected Emails Emails sent from a record page, and emails teammates sent to contacts from their own mailbox. Emails sent by sequences are listed under "Sequence" Meetings Meetings logged on a record, and finished calendar events with contacts from a teammate's calendar Tasks completed Tasks completed in the period, credited to whoever completed them Notes Notes written in the period Everyone on the access allowlist is listed, including people with nothing logged. A call or meeting counts on the day it took place, not the day it was entered. "Export CSV" downloads the table for the chosen period. Email and meetings are picked up automatically for teammates who have connected their account; calls made on a phone are only counted once someone logs them. Any view can be exported as CSV, and CSV files can be imported: columns are matched to fields by key or label, select values by option label, and relations by the related record's title. An import is limited to 1,000 rows and doesn't fire automations. Actions Buttons on the record page: run targets (shared with automations): Target What runs swirls:<workflow> A deployed Swirls workflow, by name. Input: { objectKey, record, actor, trigger }. See Swirls. campaign:<key> Enrolls the record in a campaign (once per record). local:<handler> A handler in src/app/extensions.ts. <kind>:<name> Any kind your extensions register. See Extending. crm:gen and server start-up check that every target resolves, so a misspelt campaign, handler or kind fails early instead of when someone clicks the button. Automations Events: <objectKey>.created,.updated,.deleted. They fire for changes made in the CRM UI and the assistant. Failures are logged and never block the change that triggered them. To change or reject a write, or to compare against the previous value, use hooks. Campaigns wait is relative to the previous step: "0m", "90m", "12h", "3d". {{field}} placeholders are filled from the record when each step sends, so edits made mid-campaign are picked up. {{unsubscribeUrl}} is also available. Before every step the record is re-read. If it was deleted or a stopWhen field matches, the sequence stops for that record. If the address is missing or on the suppression list, that one email is skipped and the next is tried when it is due. See Campaigns for delivery, unsubscribes and operations. Marketing website is the business's site, as an https:// address. It is the only required part. tags are the tracking tags the business uses, by id: gtm, ga4, googleAds, metaPixel, linkedinInsight. Each id must be in its vendor's form. channels are where posts can go. network is linkedin, facebook, x, or one your app adds. ads are the ad accounts whose results are shown. network is meta, google, or one your app adds. via on a channel or an ad account says who calls the network: "direct" (the CRM, the default where it can) or "swirls" (a workflow). With this block the sidebar gains a Marketing page. marketing can no longer be used as an object's key. See Marketing. The assistant's page assistant changes how the Ask page presents the assistant. What the assistant can do is not set here: that is its tools, in swirls/assistant.swirls (see Swirls). Key Description name What the assistant is called on the page: the box says "Ask ". Default "Assistant", up to 40 characters. greeting The line a new chat opens with. Default "What can I help with?". suggestions Up to six prompts offered under the box of a new chat. label is the button (up to 40 characters); prompt is what gets asked when it is pressed. Without any, the page writes four from the first object in objects.

description: Most changes are config: see the configuration reference. When config isn't enough, extend in code. Server-side extensions live in one file you own, src/app/extensions.ts:

Run targets: add a new kind

Integrations: let teammates connect another service
Files: choose where a record's folder goes
Pages and endpoints of your own

text: Extending Most changes are config: see the configuration reference. When config isn't enough, extend in code. Server-side extensions live in one file you own, src/app/extensions.ts: The full contract, with types, is packages/spools/src/crm/extensions.ts. Handlers: run your own code from a button or automation ctx is { objectKey, record, actor, trigger }. Import updateRecord and friends from @swirls/spools/extensions so hooks and automations still run. The returned message is shown to the user. Hooks: react to record changes Hooks run for every write, whether it comes from the CRM or the assistant. Available hooks: beforeCreate, afterCreate, beforeUpdate, afterUpdate, afterDelete. beforeUpdate and afterUpdate receive the previous record. Values returned from a before* hook are still validated against the config. A change happens in this order: The before* hook runs. Throwing here refuses the change: nothing is written, and staff see the message. The record and its lines on the timeline are written together, as one transaction. The after* hook and the config's automations run, once the change is kept. So an after* hook can read the record it is told about and change it again. If it throws, the change stays, and staff see "Saved, but a step after it failed" with the message, so nobody makes the change a second time. For simple "when X changes, run Y", prefer automations in the config. Use hooks when you need the previous value, want to change or reject the write, or need logic that doesn't belong in a workflow. Hand a record on to the next step A hook can create the records and tasks the next person needs. Import from @swirls/spools/extensions: its createRecord and updateRecord write through the service, so the new records get their own timeline, hooks and automations, and createTask makes the to-dos. (The framework's own modules return Effects, which do nothing when awaited; this file is their promise version.) A hook that updates the record it is handling runs again for that update: compare with previous (as above) so it does its work once. actor is null for scripts; a CSV import in the CRM has the teammate who ran it. Decide what a hand-off should do with no actor; bulk imports that call records.createRecord directly skip hooks. To give the new record the old one's folder, see shareRecordFolder in Files. Run targets: add a new kind A run target kind handles every "<kind>:<name>" in the config. validate is optional. When present, bun run crm:gen and server start-up use it to reject targets that can't resolve, so a typo fails early. Email: use a different provider Campaign email goes through the Spool's email adapter. To send it some other way without writing an adapter, replace the transport: Keep the headers: they carry the one-click unsubscribe. Marketing: add a social or ad network Add a network under marketing and a channel or an ad account in crm.config.json can name it. posts networks say how long a post may be and how to send one; ads networks say how to read an account's campaigns. The full example is in Marketing. Integrations: let teammates connect another service Add an OAuth provider under integrations and it appears on the Integrations page. The framework runs the connect flow and keeps the tokens encrypted; your handlers ask for a current token with getAccessToken. The full example is in Integrations. Files: choose where a record's folder goes An object with files in the config gives each record a folder in the drive, at <plural label>/<record title>, or inside a related record's folder with under. Return another path from files.location to lay the drive out your way. It is asked once per record, when its folder is made. See Files. Add a field type A field type is part of the framework, so this is a change to packages/spools: two files, and the compiler lists what's missing. In packages/spools/src/crm/field-types.ts, add the config shape to fieldSchema and an entry to fieldTypes: In packages/spools/src/crm/ui/fields.tsx, add rating to fieldDisplay and fieldInput. Then run bun run crm:gen, and document the type in docs/configuration.md. Add a view type Add the config shape to viewSchema in packages/spools/src/crm/config-schema.ts. Add a component to viewComponents in packages/spools/src/crm/ui/views.tsx. Its props are ViewProps in the same file. Teach sanitise in packages/spools/src/server/views.ts which settings the new type keeps. Pages Each page is a small file in src/routes that mounts one of the framework's: Delete the file and the page is gone. Keep its data and change how it looks: Pages and endpoints of your own A page is a route file. Inside src/routes/_crm it gets the CRM's shell, and only signed-in teammates can open it. The framework's parts are in @swirls/spools/ui/* ( kit for buttons and dialogs, shell for the top bar, workspace, views). Its data comes from a server function, whose handler is one from @swirls/spools/handlers: An endpoint is the same with apiRoute: Handler Who it answers crmHandler A server function, for signed-in teammates on the access list apiRoute An endpoint, for the same people. Anyone else gets 401 cronRoute A scheduled job with CRON_SECRET. Anyone else gets 401 publicHandler A server function that answers anyone. Nothing staff-only belongs here publicRoute An endpoint that answers anyone, such as a webhook. Check its signature before anything else Each checks who is asking before your code runs, hands it the person, stops when the browser goes away, and shows the page the message of an error you throw. A new Spool's bun run lint refuses a server function or endpoint that goes without one. Theme the CRM The CRM's colours are CSS variables on.crm, defined in packages/spools/src/crm/ui/theme.css. Override them in your own src/styles.css, after the theme import, instead of editing the theme file: The CRM follows the system light or dark setting until someone uses the toggle in the sidebar. Give the assistant a new capability Add a tool to tools in packages/spools/src/server/tools.ts with a Zod input schema. Add a tool workflow to swirls/assistant.swirls that posts to /api/swirls/tools/<tool>, and list it in the agent's tools. Run swirls doctor, then swirls deploy.

title: Search and filters
description: How people find things in the CRM, and how it is built. The first half is what the app does; the second is for whoever changes it.
text: Search and filters How people find things in the CRM, and how it is built. The first half is what the app does; the second is for whoever changes it. Search Filters Sorting Views and links Keys In the config How it works Limits Search Cmd+K (Ctrl+K) opens search from any page. On a narrow screen it is the magnifying glass in the top bar. It finds By Records of every object Their title and every searchable field Notes Title and body Emails, calls and meetings Subject or summary, and body Tasks Title Files File and folder names (when a file store is set up) Pages, views and "New …" Name With nothing typed it lists the records you opened most recently (kept in the browser you are using) and your favourites. Order. Records come first, best match first: the whole title, a title that starts with what you typed, a word in the title that starts with it, a title that contains it, another field that contains it, then near-misses. A near-miss is one wrong, missing, extra or swapped letter in a word of four letters or more, so acem finds "Acme". Ties go to what you opened recently, then to what changed most recently. Every word you type must match somewhere. Accents and capitals are ignored. Digits typed like a phone number match however the number was stored: 4105550101 finds "(410) 555-0101". Groups. "Best matches" (when more than one kind of record matches), one group per object, then Notes, Emails and calls, Tasks and Files. A group shows five results and a "Show all" row that opens the object's list with the search applied. Each record shows a second line that tells it from others of the same name (the first short columns of the object's table view) or, when the match was not in the title, the field and text that matched. Notes, emails, calls, tasks and files appear a moment after you stop typing, under what is already shown. In their text, word endings don't matter ("cabinets" finds "cabinet") and the last word may be unfinished. Tab narrows the search to one object: the one whose name you typed, or the one the highlighted result belongs to. Filters Every list has one box for searching and filtering. Typing narrows the list as you go. When what you type can be read as a filter, the box offers it: Type It offers won Stage is Won dana Owner is Dana chicago City is Chicago, with how many records smith Contact is John Smith >5000, over 5k, 5000-10000 Value > 5,000 and so on this month, last 30 days, over 30 days ago on each date field no email, has owner, no deals Email is empty, and so on stage won, close date next week, last contacted over 30 days ago the named field with that value city Filter by City… (opens its editor) Tab takes the first offer, or the highlighted one. When the text can only be a filter ( >5000, no email, an option's whole name) the offer is highlighted already and Enter takes it. The Filter button, or F, lists every field. A column's heading offers "Filter by this column". Click a filter to change its operator or value, and its × to remove it. Operators Field type Operators text, longtext, email, phone, url contains, does not contain, is, is not, starts with, ends with, is empty, is not empty number, currency =, ≠, >, ≥, <, ≤, is between, is empty, is not empty date, datetime, Created, Updated is, is before, is after, is between, in the last N days, in the next N days, more than N days ago, is empty, is not empty select, relation, user, Created by is any of, is none of, is empty, is not empty boolean is yes, is no "Is", "is before" and "is after" take a date or a period: today, yesterday, tomorrow, or this, last or next week, month, quarter or year. A period is kept as written and worked out each time the list loads, in the time zone set by app.timezone, so a view of "closing this month" is always this month. Weeks start on Monday. Text is matched whatever its case. "Is not", "does not contain" and "is none of" include records where the field is empty. For a teammate field, Me stands for whoever is looking, so one shared "My deals" view works for everyone. Activity Every object has three dates the CRM keeps for you. They filter, sort and show as columns like any date field. Field What it is Last activity The most recent call, meeting, email, note or task on the record Last contacted The most recent call, meeting or email. An email that was drafted but not sent doesn't count Next task due The earliest due date among the record's open tasks "Not contacted in 30 days" is Last contacted more than 30 days ago; "never contacted" is Last contacted is empty; "no next step" is Next task due is empty. Field edits and automations don't count as activity. Through relations A field of a related record. Open a relation under "Fields of related records" in the Filter list, or type both names ("company ind"): Company › Industry is Finance shows deals whose company is in finance. A deal with no company is treated as a deal whose company has nothing in that field: it matches "is empty", "is not", "is none of" and "does not contain", and nothing else. Records that point here. Under "Related records": has any deals, has no deals, optionally only those where some condition holds ( has deals where Stage is Won). Both go one step: not the company's owner's team, and not a condition through a relation inside "has deals where". A list takes up to 4 sets of filters, 10 filters in a set, 5 conditions inside one "has … where", and 40 conditions in all. Past that the Filter button is disabled, and a link that carries more is cut back to that many. Combining Filters side by side must all hold. One filter can hold several values ( Stage is Won or Lost). or starts a second set: a record is shown when it meets every filter of either set. Encrypted fields A field marked encrypted can only be asked what its mode will be able to answer once encryption is in force: Mode Filters Search storage is empty, is not empty no eq those, and is, is not no match is empty, is not empty, contains, does not contain yes search all yes The values the filter box offers as you type ("City is Chicago") come only from unencrypted fields and ones marked search. Sorting The Sort control, or a column's heading, sorts by any column, including a relation (by the related record's title) and the activity dates. Up to three levels: "Then sort by this" adds one. Empty values go last in either direction. Views and links Filters and sort you change are tried, not saved: they go in the page address. So a filtered list can be bookmarked or sent to a colleague, Back undoes the last change, and nobody else's view changes under them. When what is on screen differs from the saved view: Save writes it to the view, for everyone who uses it. Save as a new view makes a view for everyone, or one only you see. Reset goes back to the view as saved. Columns, board cards and footer calculations are still saved as you change them. CSV export, footer calculations and boards all follow the filters on screen, and a record created from a filtered list starts out matching it when the filters pin a field to one value. Keys Key Where Does Cmd+K / Ctrl+K anywhere Open search ↑ ↓, Enter search, filter box Move, choose Cmd+Enter search Open in a new tab Tab search Narrow to one object Backspace in an empty box search Search everything again / a list Put the caret in the filter box F a list List the fields to filter by Tab filter box Take the first or highlighted offer Backspace in an empty box filter box Remove the last filter Esc either Close the list, then clear the box In the config Mark the fields people will look things up by as searchable: phone numbers, addresses, reference numbers. Set the business's time zone once: A view's filters is where the view starts. The short form pins fields to one value; the long form is a list of conditions, all of which must hold; a list of lists matches when any one list does. op Field types value contains, notContains, is, isNot, startsWith, endsWith text-like a string eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte number, currency a number between number, currency, date, datetime [low, high] on, before, after date, datetime "YYYY-MM-DD" or a period: today, yesterday, tomorrow, thisWeek, lastWeek, nextWeek, and the same for Month, Quarter, Year inLast, inNext, olderThan date, datetime a number of days in, notIn select, relation, user a list of option values, record ids or user ids ( "@me" for the viewer) yes, no boolean none empty, notEmpty any none has, hasNone ~object.field none; optional where: conditions on those records field is a field key, a system column ( createdAt, updatedAt, createdBy, lastActivityAt, lastContactedAt, nextTaskDue), relation.field for a field of a related record, or ~object.field for the records of object whose relation field points here. crm:gen rejects a condition the app would not apply. sort takes one { "field", "dir" } or a list of up to three. The assistant's crm_search tool takes the same conditions as filters. How it works Piece Where What a condition is, operators per field type, relative dates, cleaning packages/spools/src/crm/filters.ts (pure, shared) Conditions to a database query packages/spools/src/server/filter-query.ts, used by listRecords and countMatching in packages/spools/src/server/records.ts Typed text to offered filters packages/spools/src/crm/suggest.ts (pure) Matching and ranking in the browser, the index store packages/spools/src/crm/search.ts (pure) Building the index, searching text on the server, value suggestions packages/spools/src/server/search.ts The search palette packages/spools/src/crm/ui/search.tsx The filter box, chips, editors and field list packages/spools/src/crm/ui/filter-bar.tsx Filters and sort in the page address, Save and Reset src/routes/_crm/$object/index.tsx Views as stored packages/spools/src/server/views.ts The activity dates refreshStats in packages/spools/src/server/records.ts Search needs no request for records. After the first page has loaded, the browser fetches every record's id, title, summary line and its short, unencrypted searchable fields once ( searchIndexFn), and keeps them in memory for the life of the tab; nothing is written to disk. Each key press is matched against that. Before the index is used again after 30 seconds, or after a change made in the tab, the browser asks only for what changed since ( updatedAt), and fetches everything again if the counts show something was deleted. Fields marked encrypted are never in the index, apart from the title, and nor are longtext fields; the server searches those. An object with more than 25,000 records has its 25,000 most recently changed in the index, and the server finds the rest. The server searches text. searchDeepFn runs a quarter of a second after typing pauses, and a request still on its way when more is typed is abandoned: records by every searchable field (which also covers what the index leaves out), notes and activities through two Postgres full-text indexes ( notes_search, activities_search, declared in packages/spools/src/crm/codegen.ts), tasks by title. Notes and activities come back newest first, with matches in the title or subject ahead of matches in the body; they are not ranked by relevance, because scoring every email that mentions a common word is slow. File names are a separate request to the file store. Filters are data, checked in one place. Whatever arrives from a page address, a saved view, the config or the assistant goes through cleanFilters, which keeps only conditions that name something the config has, with an operator the field's type and encryption mode allow and a value of the right shape. The rest is dropped (the assistant's tool reports it instead). The query builder then only ever sees conditions it can express. The activity dates are columns ( last_activity_at, last_contacted_at, next_task_due) on every object's table. refreshStats recomputes a record's three from its activities and tasks whenever one is written; it does not touch updated_at. To fill them for records that existed before, run it once per object without a record id (see Upgrading). Limits Tables show 50 records a page and boards up to 500 cards. Relations are followed one step, in either direction. A filter is limited in size (see Through relations), because every condition is a test on every record and a filter fits in a link. The limits are in packages/spools/src/crm/filters.ts. They bound what one request can ask; they are not a substitute for a statement timeout on the database role. No roll-up filters ("more than three deals") and no saved lists of records apart from views. File search covers names, not contents. Recently opened records are remembered per browser, not per person. Without database indexes on text columns, "contains" reads every row of the object. That takes a few milliseconds for thousands of records. Past a few hundred thousand, add trigram indexes ( pg_trgm) on the searchable columns.

title: Campaigns
description: Campaigns are durable email sequences defined in crm.config.json (see the reference): a few emails with waits between them. Each record that is enrolled has one row in the database saying which email is next and when it is due, so a three-week sequence survives deploys and restarts, and runs the same on a server and on a serverless host.
text: Campaigns Campaigns are durable email sequences defined in crm.config.json (see the reference): a few emails with waits between them. Each record that is enrolled has one row in the database saying which email is next and when it is due, so a three-week sequence survives deploys and restarts, and runs the same on a server and on a serverless host. Enrolling records Add an action with "run": "campaign:<key>" to the campaign's object, or an automation such as { "on": "contacts.created", "run": "campaign:onboarding" }. A record can be enrolled in a campaign only once; repeat clicks do nothing. Every enrollment, send and skip is written to the record's activity timeline. Sending Email goes through Resend. Set RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM, an address on a domain you've verified in Resend. Without them, steps still run and are recorded on the timeline as "logged (email not configured)", which is handy in development. Every email includes: an unsubscribe link at APP_URL, signed with APP_SECRET ( /unsubscribe?t=...). Without both, sequence email is not sent: an email with a dead unsubscribe link must not go out List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers, so mail clients show a one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) Suppression Addresses in the email_suppressions table never receive campaign email. They're added when someone unsubscribes or, once the webhook is configured, when an email bounces or gets a spam complaint: In Resend → Webhooks, add {APP_URL}/api/webhooks/email for the events email.bounced and email.complained. Set RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET to the webhook's signing secret. Suppression applies to campaigns. Swirls workflows send their own transactional email and don't consult this list. Sending hours By default an email goes out when it is due, whatever the hour. To keep later emails to working hours, set app.sendingHours in crm.config.json: The hours are on the clock of app.timezone, Monday to Friday unless you add "weekdaysOnly": false. An email that falls due outside them waits for the next opening: later that morning, the next morning, or Monday. An email with no wait is always sent at once, because someone has just asked for it. Operations State is the sequence_runs table: one row per enrolment, with the next email, when it is due, and whether the run is active, finished or stopped. Nothing is kept in memory or on disk. What sends. tick in packages/spools/src/server/campaigns.ts sends every email that is due. A server that stays up calls it once a minute. A serverless host has no process to keep a timer in, so with SERVERLESS=1 a cron job calls /api/cron/sequences with CRON_SECRET as a bearer token. An email goes out within one interval of being due. An email with no wait is sent in the request that enrolls the record. Any number of instances. Two instances, or a cron job overlapping the last one, can't send the same email: each run is taken with a single conditional update that only one of them wins. Failures. A send that fails is tried again about ten minutes later, up to five times; then the run stops and the record's timeline says so. Every try at one email carries the same idempotency key, which Resend uses to drop a repeat, so an email that did go out before a crash is not delivered twice. A transport of your own ( email.send in src/app/extensions.ts) is handed the key as idempotencyKey. Stopping. A run stops when the record is deleted or a stopWhen field matches. A missing or suppressed address skips that one email. Changing a campaign. A run in flight reads the campaign from the config each time an email is due, by step id: edit a subject or body and the next email uses it. A run whose next step was removed stops. Avoid renaming step ids while runs are active. Without a scheduled job on a serverless host only emails with no wait are sent; the Workflows page says "Sequences need a scheduled job on this server".

title: Mailbox: email and calendar from the sign-in
description: Teammates who sign in to the CRM with Google or Microsoft can let it use that same account: mail and meetings with known contacts are logged on those contacts' timelines, and emails written in the CRM go out from the teammate's own mailbox.

sections.title: To confirm on a first live run

text: Mailbox: email and calendar from the sign-in Teammates who sign in to the CRM with Google or Microsoft can let it use that same account: mail and meetings with known contacts are logged on those contacts' timelines, and emails written in the CRM go out from the teammate's own mailbox. For that account there is no "connect your account" step and the CRM stores no tokens. The auth provider holds them; the CRM asks it for a teammate's current token each time it needs one. A teammate can also connect other mailboxes (a second address, a shared inbox, or their only one if they sign in with an email and password) on the Integrations page. Those are read and sent from in exactly the same way; only where the tokens live differs. Status: built and tested against stubbed Clerk, Google and Microsoft APIs. It has not yet been run against live accounts. The points marked "to confirm" below are the ones a first live run should check. What it does An email the teammate sent to a contact "sent an email: subject ", with a short preview. Counts as an email for the sender An email a contact sent them "received an email: subject ", with a short preview. Shown on the timeline, not counted A finished calendar event with a contact "had a meeting: title ". Counts as a meeting for each teammate who attended An email written with "Compose email" on a record Sent from the teammate's mailbox, so it is in their Sent folder and replies come back to them Only mail and meetings involving an address that is already on a CRM record are kept, and only the subject, a short preview and the time. Message bodies are never fetched, and everything else in the mailbox is read past. An email between colleagues that copies a contact is logged once, from the sender's mailbox. Nothing is logged twice: each entry carries the email's Message-ID or the event's id. An email sent from the CRM is logged at once and then matched to the mailbox's copy when the next read meets it. A teammate with no mailbox that may send (no Google or Microsoft sign-in, no connected mailbox, or no send permission) still sends through the app's email provider (Resend). The composer says so when their mailbox should have worked and didn't. A teammate with more than one mailbox that may send picks which in the composer's From row. Campaign emails always go through the app's email provider. Each teammate sees what their mailboxes allow under the envelope button at the bottom of the sidebar and on the Integrations page, with a "Read now" button and the last error if a read failed. Setup For the sign-in account, all of it is in Clerk and the provider's console; the CRM needs no keys of its own. (Connecting further mailboxes has its own setup.) Use your own OAuth credentials in Clerk. In the Clerk dashboard, open the Google or Microsoft social connection, turn on Use custom credentials and enter the client ID and secret from step 2 or 3. Clerk cannot hand out tokens for connections on its shared development credentials. Google. In Google Cloud, create an OAuth client (Web application) with Clerk's redirect URI, enable the Gmail and Calendar APIs, and add the scopes below. Publish the app ("In production"), or make it internal to your Workspace; an app left in testing is limited to its test users. Microsoft. In Microsoft Entra, register an app with Clerk's redirect URI and add the delegated Graph permissions below. Clerk signs in through the common audience, so the registration has to accept accounts from any organisation; who may use the CRM is still decided by access in crm.config.json. Your tenant may need an administrator to consent to the mail permissions. Add the scopes to the Clerk connection (the Scopes field appears once custom credentials are on): Provider To read To send Google https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send Microsoft Mail.Read, Calendars.Read (and offline_access) Mail.Send The list lives in packages/spools/src/crm/mailbox.ts. Reading and sending are checked separately, so you can grant only one. Teammates who signed in before the scopes were added reconnect once: the mailbox panel's "Open profile" button opens their Clerk profile, which asks for the extra permissions. The schedule Mailboxes are read every MAILBOX_SYNC_MINUTES (default 5; 0 turns the schedule off), the first time going back MAILBOX_LOOKBACK_DAYS (default 30). Accounts that have waited longest go first. The schedule is a timer in the server process. On a host with no long-lived process ( SERVERLESS=1) the timer is off. Set CRON_SECRET (16+ random characters) and have a cron job call /api/cron/mail-sync with it as a bearer token. Each call reads for about 45 seconds and leaves any remaining accounts for the next call. It answers 401 without the right token and 503 when Clerk cannot provide tokens at all. To confirm on a first live run That the token Clerk returns for Microsoft works against Microsoft Graph with the mail scopes, and still works days later (Clerk fetches a fresh token when asked; it needs a refresh token from the provider to do so). That Clerk obtains a Google refresh token. Google only gives one when offline access is requested. Clerk's rate limit for retrieving tokens, with every teammate read every few minutes. Troubleshooting What you see What it means "Clerk is using its shared development credentials" Step 1 is not done for that provider "No access to read your mail and calendar yet" in the panel The account hasn't granted the read scopes: step 4, then the teammate reconnects "… denied access (401/403). Reconnect the account" The grant was revoked or is too narrow; the teammate reconnects from their profile, or on the Integrations page for a mailbox they connected there The panel says there is no mailbox The teammate signed in with an email and password or another provider. They can connect a mailbox on the Integrations page "Sent from the shared address, not your mailbox" after sending Their mailbox refused the send; the reason follows, and the email went through the app's provider instead

title: Integrations: accounts teammates connect
description: The Integrations page ( /integrations) is where a teammate sees every account the CRM works with on their behalf, and connects more:
text: Integrations: accounts teammates connect The Integrations page ( /integrations) is where a teammate sees every account the CRM works with on their behalf, and connects more: The account they sign in with. A Google or Microsoft sign-in is a mailbox already; nothing is connected and the CRM stores no tokens for it. See Mailbox. More mailboxes. A second address, a shared inbox, or the only mailbox of someone who signs in with an email and password. Google and Microsoft are built in. Other services your app adds, such as an accounting or phone system. See Add a provider. The accounts your marketing posts through (LinkedIn, X, Google Ads), once a channel or an ad account in the config uses one. These are shared: whoever connects one, any teammate can publish through it from the Marketing page. See Marketing. Each person connects their own accounts. Nobody else can see or remove them, and nobody else can use them, except a marketing account, which is connected for the team. Status: built and tested against stubbed providers and a stand-in for CipherStash. It has not yet been run against live Google, Microsoft or CipherStash accounts. Connected mailboxes A connected mailbox is treated exactly like the sign-in one: Its mail and finished meetings with known contacts are logged on timelines, on the same schedule, credited to the teammate who connected it. Only the subject, a short preview and the time are kept. The teammate can send from it. "Compose email" shows a From choice when they have more than one mailbox that may send. Left alone, the CRM uses the address it knows them by, then their sign-in, then a connected mailbox. A person can connect several mailboxes, including several from one provider. Connecting the address you already sign in with is harmless: the CRM uses whichever of the two has the access it needs, and the sign-in when both do. This is also the way to give the CRM mail access without adding the mail scopes to your Clerk connection. When a teammate is removed from access in crm.config.json, their connected mailboxes stop being read. The stored tokens stay until they are disconnected or the rows are deleted. Connecting asks for the scopes listed in packages/spools/src/crm/mailbox.ts (read mail and calendar, send mail), the same ones the sign-in uses. How tokens are stored The sign-in's tokens stay with the auth provider. A connected account's tokens are the CRM's to keep, so they are sealed by the vault: by default with CipherStash ( @cipherstash/stack) inside the app before they are written to the integrations table, each value under its own key from ZeroKMS. The database only holds ciphertext, so a database dump or a leaked backup cannot be used to read anyone's mail. There is no plaintext fallback. Without its keys the vault refuses to store anything and the page says more accounts can't be connected yet. The code is in packages/spools/src/server/runtime/vault.ts. Disconnecting asks the provider to revoke the token where it offers that, and deletes the stored copy either way. Setup The sign-in mailbox needs none of this. To let teammates connect more accounts: 1. The vault With vault: aes() there is one thing to set, a key of your own: VAULT_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32). Keep it somewhere other than the database: whoever has both can read every connected account. To change it, put the old key in VAULT_OLD_KEYS so what it sealed still opens. With vault: cipherstash(): Create a workspace and an access key, then set: APP_URL (the public address of the app) and APP_SECRET (32+ characters; signs the OAuth state) must be set too. 2. Google In the Google Cloud console, create an OAuth client of type Web application. It can be the same client your Clerk connection uses, with one more redirect URI. Authorised redirect URI: {APP_URL}/api/integrations/google/callback Enable the Gmail API and the Google Calendar API for the project. OAuth consent screen: for a Google Workspace organisation choose Internal, which needs no review by Google. An External app that asks for Gmail scopes must pass Google's verification before people outside your test-user list can connect. 3. Microsoft In Microsoft Entra, register an application with a Web platform (or add the redirect URI to the one your Clerk connection uses): Redirect URI: {APP_URL}/api/integrations/microsoft/callback API permissions (delegated): openid, email, offline_access, User.Read, Mail.Read, Calendars.Read, Mail.Send. Some tenants require an administrator to consent. Create a client secret. A provider is offered once its client id and secret are set; you can set up one and not the other. The server logs which parts are on at start-up. How connecting works Connect opens /api/integrations/<provider>/connect. It checks the CRM session, sets a ten-minute, HttpOnly cookie holding a nonce and a PKCE verifier, and redirects to the provider with a signed state that names the teammate. The provider returns to /api/integrations/<provider>/callback. The callback is accepted only if the state signature is valid and unexpired, it names the signed-in teammate, and the cookie's nonce matches: so it only completes in the browser that started it. The code is exchanged for tokens (with the PKCE verifier), the account is identified, the tokens are encrypted and the row is written. Connecting the same account again replaces its tokens. getAccessToken(connectionId) (from @swirls/spools/extensions) returns a valid access token, refreshing it when it is about to expire. If the provider turns the refresh down (the person revoked access, or a password change invalidated it), the connection shows "Needs reconnecting" and is left alone until it is connected again. A provider that is merely unavailable is tried again later. Add a provider Anything that speaks OAuth 2 with the authorization-code flow can be added in integrations in src/app/extensions.ts. The framework shows it on the page, runs the flow, encrypts and refreshes the tokens. Your code decides what to do with them. Register {APP_URL}/api/integrations/<id>/callback as the redirect URI with the provider. The provider must issue a refresh token; a connection without one is refused. For a provider that only gives a long-lived access token, set refreshToken: 'optional': the connection then works until that token runs out, and shows "Needs reconnecting" after. An id is lower-case letters, digits, - or _. google and microsoft are taken. A provider with a bad id is left out, with a warning at start-up. findConnections and getAccessToken are for server code. Never return a token, or another teammate's connection, to the browser. Troubleshooting What you see What it means "More accounts can't be connected yet" The list under it names what is missing: APP_URL, APP_SECRET or the CS_* variables "… hasn't been set up for this CRM yet" That provider's client id and secret are not set "That sign-in link expired or was opened in another browser" The consent screen was left open for more than ten minutes, or finished in a different browser. Connect again "… didn't grant ongoing access" The provider sent no refresh token. Remove the CRM from the account's connected apps, then connect again "Needs reconnecting" The provider turned the stored grant down. Reconnect and pick the same account "The CRM already reaches this mailbox through your sign-in" The connection duplicates the sign-in account and is not used. Disconnect it, or leave it

title: Marketing: the website, social posts and ads
description: The Marketing page ( /marketing) is where the team sees how the business shows up outside the CRM:

sections.title: Set up a network to be reached directly
Set up a network to go through Swirls

text: Marketing: the website, social posts and ads The Marketing page ( /marketing) is where the team sees how the business shows up outside the CRM: Website. Which tracking tags the site carries, the code to paste for the ones it is missing, and what the assistant has learned about the business from it. Posts. Drafts for each social channel, a time to send each one, and what went out. LinkedIn, X and Facebook pages work out of the box. Ads. What each campaign spent and brought in over the last 30 days, for Meta Ads and Google Ads. The page appears once crm.config.json has a marketing block. A website is enough to start: Status: built and tested against stand-ins for every network, the agent engine and the website. Nothing here has been run against a live LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Meta Ads or Google Ads account yet. Send a test post to each channel before you rely on it. How a network is reached A channel or an ad account names a network. Each network is reached one of two ways: Directly. The CRM calls the network's API itself. This is the default for the networks below, and it needs no agent engine. Through Swirls. A workflow of your Swirls project calls the network and answers through the tool API. The account is then a Swirls connection, and the CRM stores no token for it. Set "via": "swirls" on the channel or ad account. network What it is Directly, the CRM uses Through Swirls linkedin Posts, page or person A teammate's LinkedIn account, connected on the Integrations page publish_linkedin x Posts A teammate's X account, connected on the Integrations page publish_x facebook Posts to a page META_ACCESS_TOKEN publish_facebook meta Ad results META_ACCESS_TOKEN ads_meta google Ad results A teammate's Google Ads account, and GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN ads_google A network that is not in this table works too: add it in your app's code, or write a workflow for it. The Marketing page says how each channel is reached and, when one is not ready, what is missing. Which to choose: reaching a network directly means registering your own app with it, as you do with Google or Microsoft for mailboxes. Going through Swirls means the app is Swirls's and you only sign in. Set up a network to be reached directly Connected accounts need the vault, APP_URL and APP_SECRET, as every integration does. A network's account is offered on the Integrations page once a channel or ad account in the config uses it. Any teammate can connect it. The account is then shared: the CRM posts through it whoever presses the button, so connect the account the business posts as, not a personal one you would not lend. Its tokens stay sealed in the vault, and no teammate can read them or remove the connection but the one who made it. LinkedIn. Create an app at linkedin.com/developers and add the products Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect and Share on LinkedIn. Posting to a company page needs the Community Management API instead, which LinkedIn reviews. Redirect address: {APP_URL}/api/integrations/linkedin/callback. LinkedIn gives most apps a token that lasts 60 days and nothing to renew it with. When it runs out the connection shows "Needs reconnecting". X. Create a project and app at developer.x.com with OAuth 2.0 turned on, type Web App. Redirect address: {APP_URL}/api/integrations/x/callback. Facebook pages and Meta Ads. In Meta Business settings, create a system user, give it the page and the ad account, and generate a token with pages_manage_posts, pages_read_engagement and ads_read. A system user's token belongs to the business and does not expire, so nobody connects anything. Google Ads. Use the OAuth client you have for Google, add the redirect address {APP_URL}/api/integrations/google_ads/callback, and enable the Google Ads API for the project. Google Ads also asks for a developer token with every call, from the API Center of a manager account. Set up a network to go through Swirls Copy examples/swirls/marketing-networks.swirls into your swirls/ folder, keep the workflows you use, run swirls deploy, and connect each account on the project's Connections page. LinkedIn and X are in the Swirls catalog. Facebook and Google Ads are providers a project gets through Composio: until yours has them, swirls doctor warns and a deploy that includes them fails. The website Tracking tags Name the tags the business uses, by id: Check the site reads the home page and compares what it carries with that list: The page says What it means On your site The tag is in the page with the id you named Not on your site You named an id and the page has no such tag. Get the code shows what to paste and where Not in the page. Tag Manager may add it The id is not in the page's source, but the page loads Tag Manager, which may add it in the browser Your site has a different one The page carries this tag with another id. One of the two is wrong Not used Neither the config nor the site has it. The card says where to find the id The code is each vendor's own install snippet with your id filled in. An id is checked against its vendor's form when the config is read, so nothing else can reach a snippet. The check reads the page as the server sends it. It does not run the page's scripts, so it cannot see inside a Tag Manager container, and it reads the home page only. The address fetched is the one in the config. Nobody using the CRM can point it elsewhere. What the business is Read the website starts the site_profile workflow. It reads the home page and keeps four things: what the business does, who it sells to, how it writes, and what it sells. The assistant reads them ( crm_marketing_context) before it drafts a post, so a draft sounds like the business. Read it again when the site changes. Posts Add the pages you post to: network account is linkedin The author's URN: urn:li:organization:<id> for a page, urn:li:person:<id> for a person facebook The page's id x The handle, for your own reference. The connection decides which account posts A post is a draft until a teammate schedules it or presses Publish now. Then: The CRM takes the post in one step that only one request can win, so two people pressing the button, or two schedulers running at once, send it once. It sends the post. Reached directly, the answer comes back in the same request. Through Swirls, the CRM starts publish_<network> and the workflow answers through post_result. The post shows Published with a link, or Not sent with the network's own words. A link gets utm_source, utm_medium=social and utm_campaign added, so analytics counts the visits it brings. Parameters the link already has are kept. A post is never sent twice by the CRM. When a post's fate is unknown (the network did not answer, or answered with a server error after the post was sent), it is marked Not sent with a note to look at the channel first: it may have gone out. A refusal the network gave in words is a plain Not sent, and can be sent again. Through Swirls, if a run starts and no answer comes back within 15 minutes, the post says so, and a teammate who has looked at the channel can say it did not go out. The assistant drafts and a person publishes. The tool API has draft_post and no way to schedule or publish. Text the assistant read (a note, an email, a web page) could have shaped the post, so each one waits for a teammate. Scheduled posts A server that stays up publishes what is due once a minute. On a serverless host ( SERVERLESS=1), point a cron job at /api/cron/marketing with Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET, as for sequences. A channel reached directly needs nothing more. For one that goes through Swirls, nobody is signed in when a scheduled post falls due, so Swirls needs a credential of its own: set SWIRLS_API_KEY. Without it the post is marked Not sent and says why. Publish now works either way. Ads account is the ad account's number: the digits after act_ for Meta, the customer id without dashes for Google Ads. Read again reads each account on its own, so one that fails leaves the others. Each read takes the account's campaigns and their last 30 days, and replaces what was held for that account. The page shows spend, impressions, clicks, click rate, results and cost per result. The CRM shows ad results and does not change ads. Budgets, bids and pausing stay in the ad network. For Meta, a result is a lead (the lead action). For Google Ads it is a conversion as the account defines one. Adding a network In your app's code Add it under marketing in src/app/extensions.ts. The key is what a channel names as its network; one of the same key as a built-in network replaces it. What publish throws is what the team reads on the post. The CRM cannot know whether a post that threw went out, so it adds the note to look at the channel first. As a workflow A channel whose network has no code is handed to Swirls. Write a workflow named publish_<network> (or ads_<network>), as in marketing-networks.swirls: its root takes the post and the channel, and its last node posts to /api/swirls/tools/post_result (or /api/swirls/tools/save_ads). Run swirls doctor, then swirls deploy.
