Open the run in Swirls, then look at the channel "The site could not be reached" The server could not fetch marketing.website. The last good check is still shown

title: Guides
description: Guides show people around the CRM. Each is a few short steps about one place (a list, a record page, the Tasks page), offered once, the first time someone is there. The first half of this page is what the app does; the second is for whoever writes or changes guides.
text: Guides Guides show people around the CRM. Each is a few short steps about one place (a list, a record page, the Tasks page), offered once, the first time someone is there. The first half of this page is what the app does; the second is for whoever writes or changes guides. What people see The built-in guides Dismissal Your own guides Places Anchors Turning offers off How it works Limits What people see An offer. The first time someone is in a place that has a guide, a small card appears in the bottom corner with the guide's name and three choices: Show me, No thanks and Don't offer guides. It does not take the keyboard and nothing under it is blocked. It waits until the page has settled, and while a dialog is open. A guide. Show me starts it. A card sits beside the thing each step is about, which is ringed; the rest of the page stays usable. Next and Back are buttons (Right and Left arrows also work while the card has the keyboard), the × closes the guide, and so does Esc. On a phone the card is a sheet along the bottom, or along the top when what it points at is low on the screen. A step about something the page doesn't have is left out: a record with no email field has no "Write an email" step. Help. The question mark at the bottom of the sidebar lists every guide, marks the ones not yet seen as New, and starts any of them again. A guide that belongs to another page takes you there first. One that needs a record says "Open any deal and … will start", and starts when you do. The same menu has Offer guides as I go, which turns offers off or back on. One guide is offered at a time. After an offer is answered or a guide ends, the page offers nothing more until you go somewhere else, so the next guide for a place comes on a later visit. The built-in guides In the order they are offered: Guide Place About A quick look around ( welcome) anywhere, first The sidebar, search, the assistant, Help Your Home page ( home) Home The ask box, record counts, your tasks, recent activity Searching ( search) Search, when it is open What it finds, narrowing to one kind of record, keys Working in a list ( list) any list Views, View settings, editing in place, New, Import / Export Filtering and sorting ( filters) any list Type to filter, the Filter button and chips, Sort, Save and Reset, totals Working on a board ( board) a list showing a board Columns, dragging, adding in a column, card fields A record page ( record) any record Details and editing, tabs and the timeline, favourites, previous and next, the ⋯ menu Keeping a record up to date ( recordActions) any record Email, calls and meetings, notes, tasks, files Tasks, Notes, Files, Reports, Workflows ( tasks … workflows) that page What the page holds and how to add to it Your mailbox and connections ( integrations) Integrations Mailboxes, what is kept, the mailbox panel The assistant ( assistant) Assistant Starting a chat, checking what it changed, earlier chats Their words use your config's labels: a list guide on deals says "deals", and the welcome names your record types. None is longer than five steps. Dismissal No thanks, finishing a guide, or closing it part-way all mean the same thing: that person is not offered that guide again, in any browser or on any device. It stays in Help. Leaving the page without answering is not an answer; the offer comes back the next time they are there. Don't offer guides stops every offer for that person, including guides added later, until they turn Offer guides as I go back on. A guide added later is new to everyone. People who finished the old ones are offered it the first time they are in its place, and it shows as New in Help. Changing a guide's words does not offer it again. To offer a rewritten guide to everyone again, give it a new id. Your own guides Guides are part of crm.config.json, under guides, by id. With a built-in guide's id you replace it; with false you turn it off; with a new id you add one. Key Required Description title yes The guide's name, in the offer and in Help. where for a new id The place it belongs to. A replacement keeps the built-in guide's place unless you set one. steps yes One to eight steps. Keep it to five or fewer. steps[].title yes A few words. steps[].body yes One or two plain sentences, at most 500 characters. No markup. steps[].target no The anchor to point at, or a list of them: the first one on the page is used. Without it the step is shown in the corner. steps[].keep no Show the step without a pointer when its anchor is not on the page, instead of leaving it out. Use it for things a layout hides, such as the sidebar on a phone. In a title or body, {record}, {records}, {Record} and {Records} become the label of the object in view ("deal", "deals", "Deal", "Deals"), or "record" and "records" on a page that has no object, and {app} becomes app.name. Order. The welcome and any other guide for anywhere come first. Then guides for one object ( list:deals, record:deals): what you say about your own records is offered before how lists work in general. Then the rest. Within each of the three, built-in guides keep their order and yours follow in the order the config lists them. bun run crm:gen (and bun run check) rejects an unknown place, an object or field the config doesn't have, an anchor that doesn't exist, a new guide with no where, and false for an id that is not a built-in guide. Write a step so that it is true whenever its anchor is on the page. If a step only makes sense for one object, put it in a guide for that object ( "where": "record:deals") rather than the generic one. Places where The guide belongs to anywhere Every CRM page. Offered before any other guide. home, tasks, notes, files, reports, workflows, integrations, assistant That page list, list:<objectKey> Any object's list, or one object's board, board:<objectKey> A list while it shows a board view record, record:<objectKey> Any record page, or one object's search Search (Cmd+K), while it is open. No other guide is offered then. Anchors An anchor is a data-guide attribute on something in the framework's pages. Where Anchors The frame sidebar, nav-search, nav-records, nav-favorites, nav:<objectKey>, nav:<page> ( nav:tasks), help, mailbox, theme, ask; with the sidebar closed, show-sidebar and open-search Home home-ask, home-counts, home-tasks, home-activity Search search-box, search-results, search-keys A list view-menu, view-settings, save-view (only while there are unsaved filters or sorting), import-export, new-record, filter-bar, filter-box, filter-add, sort; on a table table and table-foot; on a board board and board-add A record record-back, record-nav (only when opened from a list), favorite, record-actions, compose-email (only with an email address), log-call, log-meeting, add-note, add-task, more-actions, record-details, field:<fieldKey>, record-tabs, tab:overview, tab:activity, tab:emails, tab:notes, tab:tasks, tab:files, tab:<objectKey>.<field> for a related list Tasks tasks-scope, new-task, tasks-list Notes new-note, notes-list Files files-path, files-search, files-add Reports report-activity, report-charts Workflows workflow-status, workflow-lists, workflow-runs Integrations mailboxes, mailbox-privacy Assistant assistant-new, assistant-chats, assistant-box, assistant-thread An anchor that is not on the page is not an error at run time: the step is left out, and a guide with no steps left is not offered. That is what lets one guide serve every object. field:<key> on a guide for all records ( "where": "record") is accepted for the same reason; on a guide for one object it must be a field of that object. Turning offers off For one person: Don't offer guides on any offer, or Offer guides as I go in Help. For one guide: "<id>": false under guides. For everyone: set CRM_GUIDES=off in the environment. Help still lists the guides and replays them. In the stubbed-sign-in harness of a clone of the repository ( bun run dev:e2e, bun run demo) offers are off unless you set CRM_GUIDES=on, so a guide never appears in the middle of a test or a demo. How it works What a guide is and which one is offered where is pure code in packages/spools/src/crm/guides.ts: the built-in guides, resolveGuides (built-in plus the config's), placeOf and inPlace, guideToOffer, shownSteps, and checkGuides, which the config schema runs. No server imports and no Zod, so the browser uses the same file. What each person has seen is the guide_progress table: one row per person and guide, with finished or dismissed, and a row with guide id * for "don't offer guides". packages/spools/src/server/guides.ts reads and writes it; the first outcome recorded for a guide stands. No page asks for it. The ids a person has seen are part of the session ( getCrmSession), which the browser already has. Offering a guide costs no request, and answering one costs a single write in the background. Only your own. The two server functions ( packages/spools/src/server/guides.functions.ts) take no user id: they use the signed-in person's, which crmHandler passes in. Only this CRM's guide ids are accepted. An answer is not lost to bad timing. The browser also keeps each answer (in localStorage, per person) until the server's own list shows it, and sends it again on the next visit. So an answer given just before a reload, or while the connection was down, still counts in that browser, and reaches the server later. The interface is packages/spools/src/crm/ui/guides.tsx: GuideProvider (mounted by the shell) decides what to show, GuideHelp is the menu. The card is a non-modal dialog, labelled by the step's title and described by its text; starting a guide moves focus to it and ending one puts focus back. Colours come from the c-* theme tokens, and nothing animates when the system asks for reduced motion. A new anchor is a data-guide="name" attribute on the element and the name added to ANCHORS in packages/spools/src/crm/guides.ts (and to the table above). Limits Guides describe and point. They don't click, type, open menus or move between pages for you, so a step can only point at what is already on screen. A step's text is plain: no links, bold or line breaks. A person who dismisses a guide in one browser can be offered it once more in another browser that was already open, until that tab's session refreshes (within about a minute of the next page change). Beyond the order described under Your own guides, an added guide can't be placed between two built-in ones. Offers appear at the bottom right, above a list's page footer. They can cover the last rows of a short window until answered.

title: Adapters
description: A Spool runs on services you choose. Each kind of service has a port, a small contract the framework asks for, and one or more adapters that provide it. You choose them in src/spool.server.ts:
text: Adapters A Spool runs on services you choose. Each kind of service has a port, a small contract the framework asks for, and one or more adapters that provide it. You choose them in src/spool.server.ts: When the server starts it logs which adapters it uses and what each still needs ( [env] Campaign email (Resend): off (set RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM)). A variable an adapter can't do without stops a production server from starting. What ships Port Import Needs Auth @swirls/spools/auth/clerk CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, CLERK_SECRET_KEY, @clerk/tanstack-react-start @swirls/spools/auth/better-auth BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, APP_URL, better-auth. See Signing in @swirls/spools/auth/dev Nothing. Refuses to run in production Database @swirls/spools/database/postgres DATABASE_URL, @effect/sql-pg. See Database @swirls/spools/database/pglite Nothing but @effect/sql-pglite @swirls/spools/database/prisma DATABASE_URL, @prisma/orm-postgres Files @swirls/spools/files/drive A Blobs: localBlobs() or s3Blobs(). See Files @swirls/spools/files/flashdrive FLASHDRIVE_API_KEY, FLASHDRIVE_DRIVE_ID Email @swirls/spools/email/resend RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM, resend Vault @swirls/spools/vault/cipherstash The CS_* variables, @cipherstash/stack @swirls/spools/vault/aes VAULT_KEY ( openssl rand -base64 32) Agents @swirls/spools/agents/swirls SWIRLS_PROJECT_ID. See Swirls The packages named here are optional peer dependencies: install the ones your adapters use. Changing one Change its line in src/spool.server.ts. Auth also has a browser half, listed in src/spool.ui.ts; the page uses the one whose id matches the server's and says so if there is none. Three things to know before changing one on a Spool with data in it: Auth. Records keep the user ids of whoever made and owns them, and those ids are the auth provider's. A new provider means new ids: owners and "created by" will not match until they are mapped over. Vault. A vault can only open what it sealed. Change it and people reconnect their accounts on the Integrations page. Files. Each record remembers which store its folder is in, so it gets a new, empty folder in the new store. Nothing is copied. Changing the database adapter between postgres and prisma is safe: they read and write the same tables. Write your own An adapter is an object with an id, a label and a layer that provides the port. Everything you need is in @swirls/spools/adapter. An email provider examples/postmark.ts: If all you want is to send email another way, email.send in src/app/extensions.ts takes a plain async function and no Effect ( Extending). A database A store answers a small set of questions about tables: find, count, insert, update, remove, plus running a program as one transaction. Implement Backend and wrap it with makeStore, which adds the time limits and typed failures every store has. For anything that speaks Postgres SQL, sqlBackend does all of it and you supply two things: a function that runs a statement, and one that runs a program as a transaction. callbackTransaction makes the second from a driver whose own transaction takes a callback: examples/bun-postgres.ts: Three promises are easy to break: update checks and changes in one step, and says how many rows it changed. Sequences rely on it so that two servers never send the same email. A transaction keeps everything or nothing. Every statement a program runs inside store.transaction must go to the transaction's connection, not the pool's, and a failure or an interruption must undo it. A record and its timeline rely on it. Values come back as the table describes them: money and days as strings, moments as Date. Columns are read in terms of the table, never of the driver. Tables of its own An adapter may keep tables in the Spool's database. Describe them with the table definitions the framework uses, list them in tables, and they are created and migrated with the rest ( bun run crm:gen): Its layer may ask for the Store. Don't make tables depend on the environment, or the schema would differ between your machine and production. Check it In a clone of the repository, run the framework's own tests on your adapter. packages/spools/tests/unit/store.test.ts is what a store promises, and TEST_STORE in packages/spools/tests/support/preload.ts puts one under the whole server: How it fits together The framework ( packages/spools/src/crm, src/server, src/pages) never imports an adapter, a vendor's SDK or your app; lint refuses it. It asks for a port ( yield* Store), and the one Effect runtime per process is built from the Spool's adapters ( packages/spools/src/server/runtime/app.ts). Tests build the same runtime with stand-ins.

title: Signing in
description: Two separate things decide who gets into a Spool.
text: Signing in Two separate things decide who gets into a Spool. The auth adapter says who someone is. You choose it in src/spool.server.ts, and its browser half in src/spool.ui.ts. The access list in crm.config.json says whether they may come in. It compares their email address, and only one the auth provider has verified as theirs, with access.allowedEmails and access.allowedDomains. Anyone else who signs in sees a page saying they have no access. Answers are kept for a minute, so taking someone off the list (or out of the provider) takes effect within one. Adapter When clerk() You want sign-in run for you betterAuth() You want it in your own database, with no outside service devAuth() Development, tests and demos. Refuses to run in production Clerk Set CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and CLERK_SECRET_KEY, and install @clerk/tanstack-react-start. Under Restrictions in the Clerk dashboard, limit sign-ups to your team; the access list is checked either way. Clerk holds the Google and Microsoft tokens of the accounts people sign in with, which is how their mail and calendar are read. It can also make the token that signs each person in to Swirls without an API key. Better Auth Better Auth runs inside your server and keeps its users, sessions and accounts in your own database. People sign in with a link sent to their address, or with Google or Microsoft. There are no passwords. Only someone on the access list is sent a link or gets an account. Install better-auth, then run bun run crm:gen and bun run db:push to create its four tables ( auth_users, auth_sessions, auth_accounts, auth_verifications). PGlite creates them itself. Variable BETTER_AUTH_SECRET Required in production: 32 or more characters ( openssl rand -base64 32). It signs session cookies and encrypts stored Google and Microsoft tokens. Changing it signs everyone out, and people reconnect their accounts APP_URL Required in production: the app's public address. People must open the app there, or signing in is refused. Cookies are marked secure when it is https GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET Adds Google. Redirect URI: <APP_URL>/api/auth/callback/google MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID, MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET Adds Microsoft. Redirect URI: <APP_URL>/api/auth/callback/microsoft MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID The one organization whose people may sign in. See below TRUST_PROXY How many proxies are in front of the server, so that rate limits count the right visitor In development all of them may be missing: the address is http://localhost:3000, and everyone is signed out when the server restarts. Links by email need an email provider in production ( RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM, or another email adapter). In development the link is written to the log. A link works once, for ten minutes. Opening it shows a page with one button, because mail filters open links to check them and would otherwise use it up. The answer to asking for a link is the same, and takes the same time, whether or not the address is on the access list. Microsoft lets any organization put any address in its own people's profiles, so an address counts only when Microsoft says who owns it. Either set MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID to your own organization, whose word is then taken, or add the xms_edov or verified_primary_email optional claim to the ID token in the app's registration. Without one or the other, signing in with Microsoft always fails. Mail and calendar. "Open profile" in the mailbox panel asks Google or Microsoft for the mailbox scopes. The account must have the address the person signs in with. If you use the Integrations page too, keep its redirect URIs ( <APP_URL>/api/integrations/<provider>/callback) on the same client. Swirls needs SWIRLS_API_KEY, because Better Auth gives no identity token that Swirls could check. Removing someone. Take them off the access list. Their row in auth_users stays and opens nothing. Sessions last thirty days from signing in, and signing out takes effect at once. Status: tested against stand-ins for Google and Microsoft, and by hand in a browser with links by email. It has not been run against live Google or Microsoft accounts. The development sign-in devAuth() signs every request in as one person: whoever DEV_AUTH_EMAIL names, or the first address the access list lets in. DEV_AUTH_SIGNED_OUT=1 shows the app signed out. A new Spool uses it until you set a real provider's keys. It refuses to run with NODE_ENV=production, and a production build leaves it out. Your own An auth adapter has a server half (a directory of people, the session of a request, and optionally middleware and endpoints under /api/auth) and a browser half (the sign-in form, the account button, signing out). Both contracts are short: packages/spools/src/server/runtime/auth.ts and packages/spools/src/crm/ui/auth.tsx. The one rule that matters is that AuthUser.email is an address the provider has verified, or null. The access list trusts it. Changing provider Records keep the user ids of their owners and of whoever made them, and the ids are the provider's. Moving to another provider gives everyone a new id, so owners, assignees, favourites and "created by" won't match until they are mapped across. Plan that before you switch a Spool people use.

title: Database
description: Records and the CRM's own tables are kept through one port, the store. Server code asks it questions in terms of tables and conditions, never SQL or an ORM, so what is underneath is a choice you make in src/spool.server.ts.
text: Database Records and the CRM's own tables are kept through one port, the store. Server code asks it questions in terms of tables and conditions, never SQL or an ORM, so what is underneath is a choice you make in src/spool.server.ts. Adapter When pglite() Trying a Spool out, development, tests. Postgres inside the server process: nothing to install postgres() Deployments. Any Postgres 15 or newer (tested on 17): Supabase, Neon, RDS, Fly, your own prisma({ contract }) The same, through the Prisma 8 client, which is a release candidate today All three pass the same integration tests, and postgres and prisma read and write the same tables. PGlite Its tables are made when it starts and kept up with the config from then on. It only adds (tables, columns, indexes); it never drops, renames or retypes anything, so a field you remove from the config leaves its column behind. A required field added to an object that already has records is left empty on them. One process can open a data directory at a time. Stop the dev server before bun run db:seed, and use postgres() where several instances run. Postgres DATABASE_URL wins. Without it POSTGRES_URL is used, which Supabase's and other hosting integrations set. sslmode=require in the URL means TLS with the certificate checked. sslmode=no-verify is TLS without checking it. POSTGRES_URL with require is relaxed to no-verify, because the Supabase pooler's chain isn't one a client trusts. On Supabase's transaction pooler (port 6543) prepared statements are turned off. Use the session pooler or a direct connection for migrations. Schema and migrations bun run crm:gen writes prisma/schema.prisma from crm.config.json, the system tables, and any tables your adapters keep. Prisma's CLI migrates a Postgres from it, whichever adapter the server uses: Every table has row-level security on with no policies, and spools harden (which db:push and db:migrate run) takes Supabase's Data API roles off them. The app connects as a privileged role. Using the store Server code in the framework, and an adapter that keeps its own tables, reach the database like this: where is columns that must equal a value, and null means empty. filter is anything else: comparisons, text, relations, full-text search ( packages/spools/src/server/store/query.ts). A row's TypeScript type follows from its table, and update and remove refuse to run with no condition. Writes that belong together go in a transaction: everything in it is kept, or none of it. A failure, a bug or the request going away undoes what the program had written. Inside one, store.lock(table, { where: { id } }) holds a row until the transaction ends, so reading a row and then writing something that depends on it can't be interleaved with someone else doing the same. Creating, changing and deleting a record are each a transaction: a record is never saved without its line on the timeline. Keep a transaction to store calls: code that reaches the store some other way (an app's hook) is on another connection and doesn't see what isn't kept yet. Your own code in src/app/extensions.ts uses the promise functions instead ( Extending): createRecord, listRecords and the rest run hooks, the timeline and automations, which the store knows nothing about. Tests Point DATABASE_URL at a database made for tests, with the schema pushed ( bun run db:push). The tests write to it.

title: Files
description: The CRM has a file browser: folders, drag-and-drop upload, rename, move and search. What it keeps files in is an adapter you choose in src/spool.server.ts:

sections.title: Setup: a drive of your own

text: Files The CRM has a file browser: folders, drag-and-drop upload, rename, move and search. What it keeps files in is an adapter you choose in src/spool.server.ts: Adapter Files are kept in drive({ blobs: s3Blobs() }) Any S3-compatible bucket, with the folders in the CRM's own database drive({ blobs: localBlobs() }) A disk on the server, with the folders in the CRM's own database flashdrive() A FlashDrive drive, which also mounts as a folder on macOS and Linux Without one, the Files pages say that files aren't set up. The Files page (in the sidebar, under Notes) browses the whole drive. A record's Files tab browses that record's own folder. Give an object a files section in crm.config.json and each of its records gets a folder. Status: tested against stand-ins for FlashDrive and S3, and against a real disk. None of them has been run against a live account yet. What you can do In either place: Open a folder, and climb back with the breadcrumbs or "Up one folder". Right-click an empty spot to add a folder or upload files. Right-click a folder or a file to open, rename, move up or delete it; a file's menu also copies its link. Every row also has a ⋯ button for the same menu and a delete button, shown when you point at it or select it. See who added each file and when. A file put in a FlashDrive drive some other way shows no name. Drag files in from your computer to upload them, onto the open folder or onto a folder in the list. Drag a file or folder onto another folder, or onto a breadcrumb, to move it. Switch between a list and a grid. The choice is remembered in the browser. With an item selected: Enter opens it, F2 renames it, Delete removes it. On the Files page, search file names across everything. The folder being shown on the Files page is in the address, so a folder can be linked to. A folder that is a record's own is marked "Record" and links to it. A folder per record A record's folder is made the first time its page is opened (or its folder is first asked for), at <object's plural label>/<record title>: Companies/Acme. folders are made inside each record's folder when it is created. Use plain names: at most 60 characters, none of / \: * ? " < > |, no leading or trailing dot or space. under names a relation field. The record's folder is made inside the folder of the record that field points to: Companies/Acme/Website redesign. A record with that field empty gets a folder under its own object's name. Two records with the same name each get a folder; the second carries the first eight characters of its id. An object without files has no Files tab and no folders. The CRM remembers which folder is a record's by the store's id for it, not its path. So a record's folder can be renamed or moved in the drive and still opens from its record; renaming the record does not rename the folder. Deleting a record leaves its folder in the drive. Deleting a record's folder, in the CRM or in the drive, is allowed: the record gets a new, empty one the next time its page is opened. To lay the drive out differently, give your app a files.location in src/app/extensions.ts. It is asked once per record, when its folder is made: When one record hands over to another (a won deal becoming a job), give the new record the old one's folder with shareRecordFolder(from, to) from @swirls/spools/extensions: both then open the same folder. The library A folder at the top of the drive holds files that belong to the business rather than to one record: price lists, templates, forms. It is made the first time the Files page is opened, as "Company files". To rename it or give it folders, add files at the top level of crm.config.json: It is an ordinary folder: anything can be added to it, and more folders can be made beside it. files can't be used as an object key: it is the page's address. Setup: a drive of your own The folders, and the name and place of each file, are rows in the CRM's database ( file_nodes). The bytes are in the blob store. After choosing drive, run bun run crm:gen and, with DATABASE_URL set, bun run db:push so the table is there. Back up the database and the blob store together: either is little use without the other. A bucket: s3Blobs() Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Supabase Storage, MinIO, or anything else with the S3 API. Keep the bucket private. Files are opened by links the server signs, which last five minutes. The bucket's CORS rules must allow PUT with a content-type header from the CRM's address, because browsers send files straight to it. Upload links last fifteen minutes. A signed link can't hold the browser to a hash, so an upload is checked by its size. Settings can be passed as options, or read from variables with other names: s3Blobs({ env: { bucket: "R2_BUCKET" } }). Bun signs with AWS_SESSION_TOKEN when it is set, whatever key it is given. Where that belongs to another key, unset it. A disk: localBlobs() Files go in.data/files unless you name a folder. It suits one server with a disk that lasts: in Docker, mount a volume. It is refused on a serverless host, which has no such disk. Uploads pass through the server, so its limit on the size of a request applies: 128 MB, which is Bun's own default ( maxRequestBodySize in server.prod.ts changes it). Size and SHA-256 are checked as the file is written, and a file appears only once all of it is there. Setup: FlashDrive The folders and files in the CRM are the drive's own, so the team can open the same ones in Finder, and whatever is put in the drive there shows up in the CRM. In the FlashDrive Console, create a drive for the CRM. Use a separate drive for development and for production. In Settings → API keys, create a Read-write key for the workspace that holds the drive. It is shown once. Set these where the server runs (never in browser code or a repository): Until both are set, the file browser says what is missing. The server logs whether the feature is on at start-up. A key belongs to a workspace, not to one drive. The CRM only ever uses the drive named in FLASHDRIVE_DRIVE_ID, but anyone holding the key can reach every drive in that workspace, so keep the CRM's drives in a workspace of their own if that matters to you. To try it without a key, in a clone of the repository, run the stand-in store and point the app at it: Every request tells the store about its caller, as FlashDrive's own SDK does: Flashdrive-Client: swirls-crm/1.1.2 and Flashdrive-Write-Protocol: server-v1. The version is the FlashDrive client contract this code was written against, not the CRM's own version. The store refuses a request from a client older than its minimum, and a write that doesn't name the write protocol, with "This client version is no longer supported". If it refuses this client under its own name, the request is sent again exactly as the SDK would send it, and the server log says so. How an upload works The browser reads the file and computes its SHA-256. startUpload (server) checks the session, reserves the upload with the store in the chosen folder, and returns where to send that one file. With a bucket or FlashDrive, the browser sends the bytes straight to the store with a link signed for it. They do not pass through the CRM server, so a host's request-size limit does not apply. With a disk, or when FlashDrive asks for it, the browser sends them to /api/files/uploads/<id>, which checks the session and passes them on. finishUpload (server) asks the store to confirm. Until then nobody is shown the file. A file added from a record's Files tab is noted on that record's timeline. The store's key never reaches the browser, only a link that is good for one upload and expires in minutes. An upload that is started and never finished is removed after a day. How a file is opened Through /api/files/<id>, which checks the CRM session. A bucket and FlashDrive get a redirect to a link for that one file. A disk gets the bytes. Anyone on the team can upload anything, and a page opened from the CRM's own address could act as whoever opened it. So only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and PDF are shown in the browser, told by the file's extension. Everything else is downloaded, HTML and SVG included, and what the uploader's browser said a file was is never repeated. What the database holds Table What it is record_folders Which folder is a record's own, so its Files tab opens there file_uploads A file on its way in, until the store confirms it file_nodes With drive: the folders and files, and where each file's bytes are Limits One file added through the CRM 1 GB, or the server's request limit with a disk Files per drop or pick 50 Shown in one folder The first 1,000 folders and 1,000 files Search results The first 200 files A FlashDrive drive 500,000 files, 1 TB, folders 64 levels deep, 10 GB in one file With FlashDrive, a deleted file stays in the store's trash for an hour. With drive, deleting is for good. Deleting a folder deletes everything in it. Two servers adding files with the same name to the same folder at the same moment can end up with two of that name. Folders, and moves, are settled between them. Who can see what Anyone who may use the CRM can see, add, rename, move and delete every file, as they can notes and tasks. Folders give no separate permissions. Whoever can open a FlashDrive drive, or holds a key to the bucket, can read every file in it. Troubleshooting What you see What it means "Files aren't set up yet" The list under it names what is missing "The file store refused this CRM's key" The key is wrong, was revoked, may not write, or doesn't reach this drive or bucket "AWS_SESSION_TOKEN is set, for another key than this bucket's" Bun would sign with it. Unset it, or use the key it belongs to "The file store could not use its disk" The server can't write to the folder files are kept in. The log has the reason "The file changed while it was being added" What arrived isn't what the browser described. Add the file again "A folder can't be moved into itself" The destination is the folder, or is inside it "The file store needs a newer client than this CRM speaks" FlashDrive has raised its minimum client version past the one this code states ( STORE_CONTRACT in packages/spools/src/adapters/files/flashdrive/client.ts). Update the CRM; the server log names the minimum it asked for "Something with that name is already there" A folder or file in that place already has the name "That changed while you were looking at it" Someone else renamed, moved or replaced it. Try again "That is no longer in the file store" It was deleted or moved out of reach in the drive. Reload the folder "The file store is full" The disk is full, or the FlashDrive plan is used up "The upload was interrupted" The connection dropped while the bytes were going. Add the file again "The file store is still working on this file" The store took longer than usual to confirm. Reload the folder in a moment

title: Swirls: workflows and the assistant
description: Swirls runs everything agentic: the AI that qualifies and enriches leads, the emails those workflows send, and the CRM assistant. The.swirls files live in swirls/.

sections.title: How the app and Swirls talk

text: Swirls: workflows and the assistant Swirls runs everything agentic: the AI that qualifies and enriches leads, the emails those workflows send, and the CRM assistant. The.swirls files live in swirls/. File What it declares secrets.swirls Secret slots: vendor keys, the app callback URL and token, email addresses schemas.swirls crm_event (what the app sends) and tool_result (what the app returns) new_contact.swirls Qualify a new contact with AI, alert the team, auto-reply to website leads, write a summary to the timeline enrich_contact.swirls Web search on a contact and summarize the results to the timeline assistant.swirls The crm_assistant agent, its eight tool workflows, and the crm_web chat channel marketing.swirls Reads the business's website for the Marketing page. See Marketing How the app and Swirls talk The app owns every read and write. Swirls never connects to the database; it calls the tool API instead ( describe, search, get, create, update, add_note). That keeps validation, hooks and the timeline in one place, and once field encryption is on, decryption happens only in the app. A record made through the tool API starts no automations: text the model read could have chosen its email address, and an automation would write to it. A teammate runs them from the record. Set up Install the CLI and sign in: Validate and deploy: Set the Swirls secrets. CRM_APP_TOKEN must equal SWIRLS_APP_TOKEN in the app's environment ( bun run init generates one): In the app environment, set SWIRLS_PROJECT_ID. Give the app a way to authenticate to Swirls. Either: OIDC federation (no stored key). In the Swirls dashboard, open the project's Auth page and register Clerk as a provider, using your Clerk Frontend API domain ( clerk.acme.com in production). Copy the project audience it shows ( swirls:aud:...). In Clerk, create a JWT template named swirls whose claims are { "aud": "<that audience>" }. The app then exchanges each signed-in user's Clerk JWT for a short-lived Swirls token, and Swirls records who started each run. See OIDC Federation. An API key. Set SWIRLS_API_KEY to a project API key. It takes precedence when set. With federation only, a run needs a signed-in person. A workflow triggered where nobody is signed in (a record created by a script, for example) is skipped and recorded as "skipped" on the timeline; set SWIRLS_API_KEY if those must run. Workflow execution and agent chat need a paid Swirls plan. Without SWIRLS_PROJECT_ID, the app skips Swirls runs and records "skipped" on the timeline. Local development Swirls runs in the cloud, and its HTTP nodes can't reach private addresses, so workflows can't call http://localhost:3000. To test write-backs locally, expose your dev server with a tunnel (for example cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000) and set crm_app::CRM_APP_URL to the tunnel URL. Add the tunnel's hostname to DEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS in.env, or the dev server will refuse its requests. Adding a workflow Write swirls/<name>.swirls with a root inputSchema: crm_event. Call back into the app with an http node to /api/swirls/tools/<tool> (copy the headers block from an existing workflow). Run swirls doctor, then swirls deploy. Reference it from crm.config.json: "run": "swirls:<name>". The app resolves workflow names to ids from the active deployment and caches them for a minute. The assistant /assistant (the Ask button in the top bar, or the box on Home) streams chat through the app ( /api/assistant) to the crm_web channel. Each message is attributed to the signed-in user. The page is laid out like the chat assistants people already know: past chats in the sidebar grouped by when they were last used, the conversation in a centred column, and the box pinned to the bottom. A chat is only made when its first message is sent, and is titled from that message. While the assistant uses a CRM tool the reply shows a quiet line ("Searched deals"), which opens into the steps it took; the records those tools returned are listed under the reply as links. Its name, greeting and suggested prompts are set under assistant in crm.config.json. Where chats are kept. Swirls keeps them; the CRM has no table for them. Whose chats a person sees depends on the credential. Without SWIRLS_API_KEY the app exchanges each person's session for a Swirls token ( OIDC federation), and each person sees only their own chats. With a project API key, chats belong to the project, so everyone sees (and can delete) everyone's. That's usually fine for a single business. The page lists the 30 most recent. What the page can and can't do with Swirls today: New chat, list, open, delete Yes. Deleting asks first, and removes the chat and its messages from Swirls Stop Stops the reply on screen. Swirls has no way to cancel a turn, so the assistant finishes in the background, and any change it was making still happens; the whole reply is there when the chat is opened again Regenerate Off for Swirls ( regenerate: false in packages/spools/src/adapters/agents/swirls/server.ts): Swirls doesn't document that the web channel answers a regenerate request, and if it ignores one the question is stored twice. "Try again" after an error is still offered Rename Not yet: Swirls has no call to change a chat's title The server side of the page is the Agents port ( packages/spools/src/server/runtime/agents.ts), the Swirls adapter behind it ( packages/spools/src/adapters/agents/swirls/server.ts), packages/spools/src/server/assistant.functions.ts and the two /api/assistant routes. What the page works out (groups, titles, tool steps, linked records) is packages/spools/src/crm/assistant.ts; its parts are packages/spools/src/crm/ui/assistant.tsx. Trying the page without Swirls. In a clone of the repository, in the stubbed-sign-in harness, set E2E_ASSISTANT=stub ( E2E_ASSISTANT=stub bun run dev:e2e). The page then talks to canned replies ( e2e/assistant-stub.ts) instead of Swirls: they stream a word at a time, run a real search against the local database so their links work, and never change a record. Type table, long, note or error for the other kinds of reply. Chats live in the dev server's memory until it restarts. The stub is only ever swapped in by vite.config.e2e.ts and refuses to run in a production build. To change what the assistant can do, edit its tools list and tool workflows in assistant.swirls, or add a tool to packages/spools/src/server/tools.ts.

title: Deployment
description: The app is one Bun server: the CRM, the API routes and the campaign runtime. Any host that runs a Docker image works (Fly.io, Railway, Render, a VM).

sections.title: A host with no long-lived process

text: Deployment The app is one Bun server: the CRM, the API routes and the campaign runtime. Any host that runs a Docker image works (Fly.io, Railway, Render, a VM). 1. Database (Supabase) Create a Supabase project. Copy the session pooler connection string (Project Settings → Database). The app keeps long-lived connections; the transaction pooler isn't needed. Apply the schema: For later changes, edit crm.config.json, then bun run crm:gen, bun run db:plan -- --name <change>, commit, and run db:migrate against production. Prisma refuses destructive changes unless you pass explicit --delete or --rename decisions: --delete Deal.budget to drop a field, --rename Deal.proposalAmount:Deal.contractAmount to keep its data under a new name. db:plan starts from the db ref ( migrations/app/refs/db.json), which bun run db:push moves forward. If you applied the last migration to your local database with db:migrate instead, the ref is still one migration behind, and the new plan branches off the old one; db:migrate then refuses it with MIGRATION.PATH_UNREACHABLE. Plan from the last migration and move the ref yourself: Commit refs/db.json with the migration. 2. Signing in This is for auth: clerk(). Signing in covers the other choices. Create a production instance, add your domain, and copy its keys. Under Restrictions, limit sign-ups to your team (the CRM also enforces access from crm.config.json). 3. Environment Set what your adapters need from.env.example. At minimum DATABASE_URL, your auth provider's keys, APP_URL and APP_SECRET. The server logs which optional features are on at startup, and refuses to start in production without the required variables. 4. Run the image Health check: GET /healthz. Fly.io example: Any number of instances can run: what is due is kept in the database, and two of them never send the same email (see Campaigns). Without Docker: A host with no long-lived process Set SERVERLESS=1. The server then keeps no timers, and cron jobs call these instead, with CRON_SECRET as a bearer token: Route What it does /api/cron/sequences Sends the sequence emails that are due. See Campaigns /api/cron/mail-sync Reads teammates' mailboxes. See Mailbox /api/cron/marketing Publishes the scheduled posts that are due. See Marketing /api/cron/warm Does one small database read, to keep an instance from going cold Files need a bucket or FlashDrive, because localBlobs() needs a disk that lasts. 5. Swirls Deploy swirls/ and set its secrets (see Swirls), with crm_app::CRM_APP_URL set to your APP_URL. Checklist bun run db:migrate (or bun run db:harden) has run, so RLS is on and the Supabase API roles have no access Supabase → Settings → API → Exposed schemas doesn't include public TRUST_PROXY matches the number of proxies in front of the app access in crm.config.json lists your domain or emails Sign-ups restricted at your auth provider APP_SECRET and SWIRLS_APP_TOKEN are 32+ random characters, unique per environment On a serverless host: CRON_SECRET set and cron jobs for /api/cron/sequences, /api/cron/mail-sync and, if you schedule posts, /api/cron/marketing Email domain verified and the delivery webhook ( /api/webhooks/email) configured Supabase backups enabled

title: Security
description: Each deployment of a Spool serves one business. This page says who can do what in one, and what to know before putting customer data in it. To report a vulnerability, see the security policy.
text: Security Each deployment of a Spool serves one business. This page says who can do what in one, and what to know before putting customer data in it. To report a vulnerability, see the security policy. Trust model These are the boundaries the code enforces: Who Can do Enforced by Anyone See the sign-in page, unsubscribe with a valid signed link The only public routes; the unsubscribe token is signed with APP_SECRET Signed-in person not on the allowlist Nothing in the CRM The boundary checks a verified email against access in crm.config.json. An auth adapter hands over an address only when its provider has verified it CRM user Read and write every record, run actions, use the assistant Every CRM server function and API route goes through the boundary ( crmHandler, apiRoute); lint refuses one that doesn't Swirls (workflows, assistant tools) Call /api/swirls/tools/* Bearer SWIRLS_APP_TOKEN (32+ chars, constant-time compare). Fails closed when unset A cron job Run one pass of the mailbox sync, the sequences or the scheduled posts, or keep the server warm, through /api/cron/* Bearer CRON_SECRET (16+ chars, constant-time compare). Fails closed when unset The email provider Report bounces and complaints to /api/webhooks/email The email adapter checks the signature (Resend: Svix, with RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET). Refused when no secret is set There are no per-user roles inside the CRM: every allowed user has the same access. Use separate deployments if you need hard separation. Things to know The development parts don't run in production. A copy with no keys uses a database inside the server and a sign-in that lets everyone in. In a build both are left out: src/spool.server.ts picks them only when NODE_ENV isn't production, which a build fixes, and the development sign-in refuses to start under NODE_ENV=production. A deployment missing its keys stops at start-up. Clerk development instances are for testing. One verifies any address ending in +clerk_test for whoever types a fixed code. A deployment never accepts such an address, and says at start-up when it is running on a development instance's keys ( sk_test_). Use the production instance's keys where real people sign in. Field encryption isn't active yet. Fields marked encrypted are stored as plaintext until @cipherstash/stack-prisma supports Prisma 8. Treat the database as holding plaintext PII and secure it accordingly. AI sees CRM data. Swirls workflows and the assistant receive record contents, including text that came from outside your team (imports, pasted notes). Treat that text as untrusted input to the model. The assistant's tools can only read and modify CRM records and add notes, and they can't change email addresses. A record made through the tool API starts no automations, so nothing emails an address the model chose. Its replies never load an image, so text it read can't have a browser send what it knows to another server. Workflows email your team. Mailboxes. For the account a teammate signs in with, the auth provider holds the Google or Microsoft tokens and the CRM asks it for one when it reads or sends. With Clerk, access to your Clerk secret key is access to those mailboxes. With Better Auth they are in your own database, encrypted with BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, so that secret together with the database is. Only the subject, a short preview and the time of mail involving a known contact are stored; message bodies are never fetched. Whose mail it is comes from the address in the From header, never the name beside it. Only the mailbox itself says a teammate sent a message: Gmail's Sent label, or Microsoft's Sent Items folder. Junk and deleted mail are read past. See docs/mailbox.md. Connected accounts. Tokens for accounts connected on the Integrations page are sealed by the vault in the app before they are stored; the database holds only ciphertext and there is no plaintext fallback. Each is sealed for the row it is stored on, and is refused anywhere else, so someone who can write to the database can't move one teammate's tokens onto a connection of their own. The vault's keys ( CS_*, or VAULT_KEY) together with the database are access to those accounts. The OAuth flow uses PKCE and a state signed with APP_SECRET that names the teammate and is tied to their browser by a cookie. A teammate removed from access keeps their stored tokens until they are deleted, but their mailboxes stop being read. See docs/integrations.md. Marketing. An account connected for marketing (LinkedIn, X, Google Ads) is the one kind of connection that is shared: any CRM user can publish through it from the Marketing page, whoever connected it. Its tokens are sealed like any other, and no browser is sent one. META_ACCESS_TOKEN is a token for the business's page and ad account: treat it as you treat the database's password. Only a CRM user can schedule or publish a post. The tool API can save a draft and nothing more, so text the assistant read can't put a post out. The website check fetches the address in crm.config.json and no other, and the install code it shows is built only from ids that match their vendor's form. See docs/marketing.md. Files. The file store's keys stay on the server; a browser is only ever given a transfer URL for the one file it is sending, or a five-minute link to the one file it is opening, after the CRM session is checked. Anyone who may use the CRM can open, rename, move and delete any file, and anyone with access to the store can read all of it: folders are not permission boundaries. With FlashDrive the key reaches every drive in its workspace. Files the server hands out itself are never run by the browser as a page of the CRM. See docs/files.md. Assistant conversations are shared across CRM users when using a project API key (see docs/swirls.md). Secrets. Every key in.env.example is server-only except CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, which is meant for the browser. Rotate SWIRLS_APP_TOKEN in both the app and Swirls together. Cross-site requests. Server functions and the assistant endpoint reject requests that don't come from the app's own origin ( csrfMiddleware in src/start.ts), so another site can't act through a signed-in user's session. Keep that middleware first if you add your own. Every answer also tells the browser not to show the CRM in another site's frame and to take each file as the type it is sent as. Send Strict-Transport-Security from the proxy in front of the server, which is where HTTPS ends. Supabase Data API. The app never uses it. supabase/config.toml doesn't expose public. Every generated table has row-level security on with no policies ( @@rls in the Prisma schema), and bun run db:push / db:migrate run spools harden, which revokes the anon and authenticated roles on every table and fails if RLS is off anywhere. On hosted Supabase, also remove public from Settings → API → Exposed schemas.

title: Upgrading
description: The framework is a package, so an update is a version:

sections.title: From a copy of the repository

text: Upgrading The framework is a package, so an update is a version: Read the changelog first. Breaking changes are listed with what to do about them. Your own files ( crm.config.json, src/, swirls/) never change under you. Versioning The framework follows semantic versioning. Before 1.0, minor versions can include breaking changes. "version" in crm.config.json is the config format version. It changes only when the format breaks, and bun run crm:gen tells you if your config is on an older one. New pages and endpoints are new route files. The changelog gives them to you to copy; until you do, the feature is off. From a copy of the repository Before Spools was a package, a CRM was a copy of the whole repository that merged updates from it. Moving one over changes no data: the tables are the same, column for column, and crm.config.json and every environment variable keep their names. Make a Spool in a folder of its own with bun create @swirls/spools, and copy what is yours over it: crm.config.json, src/app, src/styles.css, swirls, migrations,.env, and any pages you added to src/routes. Keep your repository's history by doing this on a branch of it. Say what it runs on in src/spool.server.ts. These are the services a copy used, so nothing behaves differently: Change your imports. In src/app/extensions.ts, '../crm/extensions' and '../server/extension-api' are both '@swirls/spools/extensions'. Change your own server code that used the database: it asks for Store instead of Database ( Database). AuthError replaces ClerkError and AgentsError replaces SwirlsError. Find a home for changes you made to the framework. Most fit an extension point: hooks, handlers, pages, or an adapter. Open an issue for one that doesn't. Run bun run crm:gen and bun run check. crm:gen should leave prisma/schema.json exactly as it was, which is how you know the database needs no change. The Resend webhook keeps its address: /api/webhooks/resend is now the same as /api/webhooks/email. The stubbed-sign-in harness reads DEV_AUTH_EMAIL and DEV_AUTH_SIGNED_OUT where it read E2E_EMAIL and E2E_SIGNED_OUT. On a host with no long-lived process, set SERVERLESS=1. It used to be worked out from the host.

title: Architecture
description: A Spool is three things put together in src/spool.server.ts: a config that describes your business, your own code, and the services it runs on.
text: Architecture A Spool is three things put together in src/spool.server.ts: a config that describes your business, your own code, and the services it runs on. The framework is a package, @swirls/spools. Your repository holds what is yours and a thin layer of files that mount the framework's pages and endpoints, so a new version is a new version number. Yours and the framework's Yours: edit freely What it is crm.config.json Your CRM: objects, fields, views, actions, automations, sequences, and your own guides src/spool.server.ts, src/spool.ui.ts Your Spool: which adapters it runs on src/app/extensions.ts Handlers, hooks, run-target kinds, email transport, integration providers src/routes/** One small file per page and endpoint. Delete one to drop a page, replace one to write your own, add as many as you like src/styles.css Brand colours and theme overrides swirls/** Your Swirls workflows and assistant scripts/seed.ts Demo data Generated: never edit Source prisma/schema.prisma, prisma/schema.json, prisma/schema.d.ts, crm.config.schema.json bun run crm:gen src/routeTree.gen.ts bun run dev or bun run build migrations/** bun run db:plan The framework: packages/spools ( @swirls/spools) What it is src/crm/** The config contract, field and view registries, the generator, the interface src/server/** Records, the service layer, the tool API, sequences, the ports and the Effect runtime ( src/server/runtime/), the store ( src/server/store/) src/adapters/** The adapters that ship with it, by port src/pages/**, src/views/** Each page's route options, and what it renders (loaded when it is opened) src/api/** The handlers behind /api/* src/cli/** The spools command If you need something the extension points don't cover, open an issue: the aim is that nobody has to patch the framework. Layers Paths on this page are inside packages/spools/src unless they start with the name of one of your own files. The boundary is where a request becomes an Effect program. A server function's handler is crmHandler(...) and a route uses an adapter ( apiRoute, cronRoute, publicRoute, toolRoute). It asks the auth adapter for the session and reads the request before the program starts, checks the access list, runs the program on the process's one runtime, interrupts it if the browser goes away, and turns a typed error into the message the page shows. See Writing server code. Ports are the only way to the outside. The framework asks for a port ( yield* Store) and never imports an adapter, a vendor's SDK or your app; lint refuses it. Each has a stand-in for tests, and its time limit and retries come from one table ( policies.ts). See Adapters. records.ts is the data layer: config-driven CRUD, search and filters. It validates every write against the field definitions. service.ts is what callers use to change records. It wraps the data layer with extension hooks, timeline entries and automations, so a change behaves the same whether it comes from the UI or the assistant. views.ts merges the views in the config with what users saved in the app, and workspace.ts holds tasks, notes, favourites, reports and CSV export. Neither goes through service.ts: they aren't config objects, so hooks and automations don't apply to them. actions.ts resolves "run": "<kind>:<name>" targets through a registry: swirls, campaign and local are built in, and extensions can add kinds. Entry points authenticate, then call the service: server functions check the session and the allowlist, and the tool API and the cron routes each check a bearer token. Your code stays plain TypeScript. Hooks and handlers in src/app/extensions.ts return promises, and the browser never loads Effect. All of the framework's server code is written with Effect. The few files that stay plain TypeScript (the Spool itself, the start-up code, the pure SQL compiler) are listed in.oxlintrc.json. Registries Three registries keep features open for extension. Each is typed so the compiler tells you what's missing. Registry File Adds Field types crm/field-types.ts (schema, column, validation) and crm/ui/fields.tsx (display, input) A new type for fields View types crm/config-schema.ts ( viewSchema) and crm/ui/views.tsx A new way to render a list Run targets runTargets in your src/app/extensions.ts A new "<kind>:<name>" for actions and automations See Extending for worked examples. Routes The CRM is served from the site root. Your src/routes/_crm/route.tsx is a pathless layout: it checks the session, loads the config and renders the shell, and its children map to / (home), /tasks, /notes, /reports, /workflows, /assistant, /<objectKey> and /<objectKey>/<id>. Because an object's key is the first path segment, keys that would shadow a built-in route ( tasks, api, unsubscribe and so on) are rejected by the config schema, and an unknown first segment is a 404. /sign-in and /unsubscribe sit outside the layout and need no session. /crm/..., where the CRM used to live, redirects to the same page at the root. Moving between pages A click should not wait for anything the browser already has: The layout's session check runs before every navigation and every link the pointer rests on, so the browser keeps the session it was given (who is signed in, the config, the team, favourites, the task count) and reuses it, checking again in the background once a minute. The same memory holds what relation pickers were given for a search, for a minute, so opening one twice asks once. It lives in crm/memory.ts and is wired up in crm/ui/session.ts. It is a convenience, not access control: every server function still checks the session itself, and nothing is remembered on the server. A page's data is reused for 15 seconds, so going back and forth costs nothing. After that the page is still shown at once, as it was, and refreshed behind ( defaultStaleTime in crm/ui/router.tsx). Data fetched when a link is hovered is used by the click that follows. Anything that changes data calls router.invalidate(), which reloads what is on screen and forgets the remembered session and titles. A change made by a teammate shows up the next time the page is fetched. A list brings back a related record's id and title only, and a board only the fields its cards show ( relations and fields in listRecords). Titles for many records are fetched together ( recordTitlesOf). Guides cost no request to offer: what each person has seen of them comes with the session. See Guides. Search matches records in the browser. After the first page has loaded, the browser fetches every record's title and unencrypted searchable fields once and keeps them in memory ( searchIndex in crm/ui/session.ts), so a key press in Cmd+K costs no request. After a change it asks only for what changed since. Notes, emails, calls and tasks are searched on the server once typing pauses. See Search and filters. A page never carries the records a relation could point at. The picker ( crm/ui/relation-picker.tsx) asks for one page of 50 titles when it is opened and searches the server as you type ( searchTitles), so an object with thousands of records costs the same as one with ten, and any of them can be chosen. A list sends the titles of the records its filters name, and nothing else. Request flow: a new record Someone creates a contact in the CRM (or the assistant does, through the tool API). The entry point checks who is asking, then calls service.createRecord. service.createRecord runs beforeCreate hooks, validates and inserts the record, writes a timeline entry, runs afterCreate hooks, then fires contacts.created automations. The swirls:new_contact automation starts a Swirls workflow with { objectKey, record, actor, trigger }. The workflow qualifies the contact with AI, emails your team, and writes its summary back through POST /api/swirls/tools/add_note, which saves a note on the record. Data model Every object in the config becomes a table with real, typed columns, plus id, created_at, updated_at, created_by, and three dates kept from the record's activities and tasks so that lists can filter and sort by them: last_activity_at, last_contacted_at and next_task_due ( refreshStats in server/records.ts). These system tables are always present ( server/store/tables.ts), and an adapter may add its own: Table Holds activities The timeline for any record. Full-text indexed ( activities_search) for search tasks To-dos with a due date and assignee, optionally linked to a record notes Titled notes, optionally linked to a record. Full-text indexed ( notes_search) for search saved_views Views created in the app, and in-app changes to config views favorites Each user's starred records email_suppressions Addresses that bounced, complained or unsubscribed mailbox_sync How far the mail and calendar sync has read each of a teammate's mailboxes. No credentials record_folders Which folder in the file store is a record's own. The folders and files themselves are in the store file_uploads A file on its way into the store, until the store confirms it integrations Accounts teammates connected on the Integrations page, with their OAuth tokens sealed by the vault before they are stored sequence_runs Each record's place in an email sequence: which email is next and when it is due guide_progress Which guides each person has finished or dismissed, so each is offered once marketing_sites What the last check of the business's website found, and what the assistant learned from it. See Marketing marketing_posts Social posts: drafts, the ones waiting for their time, and what went out marketing_ads Each ad campaign's results as last read from its network All tables have row-level security enabled with no policies. The app connects as a privileged role, which bypasses RLS. Supabase's Data API roles get nothing.

sections.title: What staff see when something fails

text: Writing server code The framework's server side ( packages/spools/src/server, src/api and src/adapters beside it) is written with Effect 4. This page is for changing it; a Spool's own code in src/app/extensions.ts is plain TypeScript, and its hooks and handlers return promises. Effect never reaches the browser. Every server module, server function and API handler is written this way..oxlintrc.json lists the few files the rules leave out, each for a reason: the runtime folder (it is where the request and the environment are touched), env.ts, spool.ts and entry.ts (which run before there is a runtime), and store/sql.ts (pure, with no database of its own). Why Failures are in the type. A function's type says what it can fail with, and the compiler won't let a server function fail with something staff can't read. Outside services have limits. Every call to the auth provider, the database, the file store, Gmail, Graph, the email provider, the agent engine and the vault has a time limit and, where repeating it is safe, retries. They are in one table: packages/spools/src/server/runtime/policies.ts. Tests swap services, not globals. A test provides a fake layer for a service; nothing is patched on a module and left behind for the next test. When the browser goes away, the work stops. The program is interrupted and its cleanup runs. The pieces File What it is packages/spools/src/server/runtime/errors.ts The errors staff can see ( Unauthorized, NotFound, Invalid, NotConfigured, DatabaseError, AuthError, Timeout) and the StaffError union packages/spools/src/server/runtime/config.ts Every environment variable, as an Effect Config, and the feature list behind the boot report packages/spools/src/server/runtime/policies.ts Time limits and retries for each outside service, and withPolicy packages/spools/src/server/runtime/adapter.ts What an adapter is: its layer, what it requires of the environment, the tables it keeps packages/spools/src/server/spool.ts defineSpool, and this process's Spool: spool(), crmConfig(), objectTable(key) packages/spools/src/server/store/store.ts Store: the database, as find, count, insert, update and remove over tables ( Database) packages/spools/src/server/store/query.ts, tables.ts, objects.ts Conditions and order as data; the system tables; an object's table, from the config packages/spools/src/server/runtime/auth.ts Auth: the auth provider's directory, with a fake ( Auth.layerTest) packages/spools/src/server/runtime/files.ts FileStore: folders, files and uploads packages/spools/src/server/runtime/agents.ts Agents: starting workflows and the assistant's chat packages/spools/src/server/runtime/http.ts The HTTP client (Effect's HttpClient over fetch) every outside service uses, and appLayer({ fetch }) for a stand-in. A request is aborted when its program is interrupted or times out packages/spools/src/server/runtime/vault.ts Vault: sealing and opening secrets, with Vault.layerTest(cipher) for tests packages/spools/src/server/sign-ins.ts SignIns: the Google and Microsoft accounts teammates sign in with, and the auth provider's tokens for them, with SignIns.layerTest packages/spools/src/server/users.ts Users: who may use the CRM, the team, sign-in accounts packages/spools/src/server/runtime/app.ts appLayer() (every service, from the Spool's adapters or a test's stand-ins), the one runtime per process, runServer for code on promises packages/spools/src/server/runtime/boundary.ts crmHandler, publicHandler, apiRoute, cronRoute, publicRoute, toolRoute: where TanStack Start hands a request to a program packages/spools/src/server/runtime/request.ts CurrentRequest: the request's headers, abort signal and session, set by the boundary packages/spools/src/server/runtime/email.ts Email: sending, and reading delivery webhooks, with Email.layerTest(sender) packages/spools/src/server/sequences.ts Sequences: the campaigns the CRM runs, from the config, with Sequences.layerTest packages/spools/src/server/extension-api.ts The framework as promises, for src/app/extensions.ts and scripts A module Export Effect.fn("module.name")(function* () {... }). The name becomes a span, so a slow request shows which call was slow. Fail with return yield* new SomeError(...), never throw. The return tells TypeScript the function stops there. Ask for a service with yield* Store. Don't import an adapter, the app, fetch, a vendor SDK or process.env: lint refuses them outside packages/spools/src/server/runtime/. Reads have a time limit and writes have none, because giving up on a write leaves its outcome unknown. To expect a particular failure, such as a unique index keeping one row, catch DatabaseError and check: The app's config and extensions come from the Spool ( spool() in spool.ts), read when they are used. Read a variable with yield* config.read(config.guidesOffered), declared in runtime/config.ts. Use Config.Redacted for secrets and Config.option for optional ones. Values are read from the environment each time, as process.env was before, so a variable set while the process runs takes effect at once. A server function crmHandler checks the session and the access list, then runs the program with the validated data and the signed-in user. There is no other way for a program to learn who is asking, and nothing inside an Effect asks the auth adapter for the session or calls getRequest(): they belong to the request, and the boundary reads them before the program starts. publicHandler is for the few functions signed-out pages call; nothing staff-only belongs there. Validators stay Zod (.validator(z.object(...))). The rule is: Zod for what comes in, Schema for what comes back. Zod checks what the browser sends and the config; Effect Schema defines errors and, as services are converted, checks what outside services answer. An API route The handlers are exported from src/api, and a Spool mounts them with a file of three lines: cronRoute refuses a request without Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET (401), answers a typed failure as JSON, and stops the run at its limit (50 s by default) with a 504. apiRoute is for routes staff call while signed in ( /api/files/*): the program gets { request, params, user } and answers with a Response. Pass signedOut to answer a signed-out visitor your own way (a redirect to /sign-in, say); by default it is 401 JSON. A typed failure the program doesn't answer itself becomes 500 JSON with its message. Type the program's input as RouteInput<{ id: string }> so params has the route's shape. publicRoute is for routes that prove who is calling some other way: a signed webhook ( /api/webhooks/email) or a token in a link (one-click unsubscribe). The program checks the signature or token first. toolRoute is for the tool API Swirls calls back into ( /api/swirls/tools/*): it refuses a request without Authorization: Bearer $SWIRLS_APP_TOKEN (401). Nobody is signed in; a tool acts as the assistant. What staff see when something fails The program fails with The page shows The server logs A StaffError Its message, exactly (see errors.ts) [server] <name> failed after <ms> ms: <tag>: <message> (not for Unauthorized) Anything else (a bug) What it threw, as before The whole cause, once, with a reference Interrupted (the browser went away) Nothing: the request is answered 499 Nothing The wording of every message staff can see is in the error's class, so a change of wording is one line in one file. A successful call slower than a second is logged as [server] <name> took <ms> ms. A new outside service A port in packages/spools/src/server/runtime/ ( Context.Service), in terms of what the CRM needs and nothing of one vendor's, with a stand-in for tests and, if a Spool can do without it, a layer that says it isn't set up. An adapter in src/adapters/<port>/<name>/server.ts. Only it imports the vendor's SDK. HTTP goes through HttpClient ( yield* HttpClient.HttpClient from effect/http), never fetch. It names what it requires and the features it switches on. A row in policies.ts: the time limit and how many retries. Retry only what is safe to repeat (reads, writes with an idempotency key), and pass withPolicy a predicate that refuses retries for answers that won't change (a 4xx other than 429). The adapter puts its provider's name to it. Its errors in errors.ts, each with a message staff can read, added to StaffError. Its option in defineSpool ( spool.ts) and its layer in appLayer ( runtime/app.ts). Promises on either side Effect code calling the app's own code. Hooks, handlers and settings in src/app/extensions.ts return promises. They are called through fromHook("files.location", () =>...) ( runtime/errors.ts), which makes a failure an ExtensionError; staff see what was thrown, as before. Promise code calling Effect code. src/app/extensions.ts and scripts import from @swirls/spools/extensions ( recordFolder, shareRecordFolder, filesConfigured, listCrmUsers, getAccessToken, findConnections,...): each runs the Effect version on the process's runtime ( runServer(program) from runtime/app.ts underneath). A typed failure rejects with the error itself, so its message still reaches the page. Don't import the framework modules from promise code: they export Effects, and await ing one does nothing. Tests Unit tests build a runtime from the app layer with stand-ins ( testRuntime(appLayer({ fetch: fake, auth: Auth.layerTest(users) })), where fake answers every outside HTTP call) or read configuration from an object ( runWithEnv({ CRON_SECRET: "..." }, program)). packages/spools/tests/unit/flashdrive.test.ts shows the file store's retries, refusals and answer checking tested that way. packages/spools/tests/unit/boundary.test.ts shows the boundary, the access list, the cron secret and the policies tested that way. Integration tests run on the app's own runtime, on the store TEST_STORE names (PGlite in the test process unless you say otherwise; Database): await run(guides.seenGuides(id)), and await failure(program) for the typed error a program fails with. To replace an outside service for the whole app (the boundary and extension-api.ts included), call await installStandIns({ fetch: fake.handle }) (and vault, signIns, auth for those services) and await installLiveServices() afterwards. One fetch answers every outside call, so route by URL when a test plays more than one provider, and read bodies with bodyText(init): Effect's client sends them as bytes; packages/spools/tests/integration/files.test.ts does this with packages/spools/tests/support/fake-file-store.ts. Each call starts from fresh services, so nothing cached leaks into the next test. packages/spools/tests/unit/guardrails.test.ts lints code written the old way with this repository's lint rules and checks that each one fires. The guardrails bun run lint (part of bun run verify) refuses, outside the files.oxlintrc.json leaves out. The rules are in packages/spools/src/oxlint: a server function handler that isn't crmHandler(...) or publicHandler(...) ( spools/server-function-handlers); anything but server functions exported from a *.functions.ts file, which browser code imports ( spools/server-function-files); an API handler that isn't a route adapter, in a route or exported from src/api ( spools/route-adapters); throw or an exported async function in packages/spools/src/server/** ( spools/effect-modules); fetch, process, @tanstack/react-start/server, a vendor's SDK, a database client, an adapter or the app in packages/spools/src/server/** outside packages/spools/src/server/runtime/ (and the last two even there); an adapter or an auth vendor's SDK in pages, which use useAuth(); effect in browser code ( packages/spools/src/crm/**, src/pages/**, src/views/**, and a Spool's routes and src/app/**). bun run build then fails if Effect reached the browser bundle anyway ( spools check-client, which looks for Effect's internal ids in dist/client).

title: API reference

text: API reference The package's entry points. Anything that isn't listed here is internal and may change in a patch release. The types are the reference for each function: your editor shows them, and the links lead to the source. Your Spool Import Exports @swirls/spools defineSpool, and the types Spool and SpoolOptions @swirls/spools/extensions defineExtensions, and the record functions for hooks and handlers @swirls/spools/handlers Handlers for your own server functions and endpoints: crmHandler, apiRoute, cronRoute, publicHandler, publicRoute @swirls/spools/oxlint Lint rules that refuse a server function or endpoint without one @swirls/spools/config-schema The config's schema, for checking a crm.config.json @swirls/spools/server serveSpool, for src/server.ts @swirls/spools/start The request middleware, for src/start.ts @swirls/spools/theme.css The styles, for src/styles.css defineSpool takes: Option Type crm the config Required. The contents of crm.config.json extensions Extensions Your hooks and handlers auth AuthAdapter Required. See Signing in database StoreAdapter Required. See Database files FilesAdapter Without it, the Files pages say files aren't set up email EmailAdapter Without it, emails are logged vault VaultAdapter Without it, no outside tokens are stored agents AgentsAdapter Without it, workflows are skipped and the assistant is off Adapters Import Exports @swirls/spools/auth/clerk clerk @swirls/spools/auth/better-auth betterAuth @swirls/spools/auth/dev devAuth @swirls/spools/auth/<name>/ui The browser half of each, for src/spool.ui.ts @swirls/spools/database/postgres postgres @swirls/spools/database/pglite pglite @swirls/spools/database/prisma prisma @swirls/spools/files/drive drive, localBlobs, s3Blobs @swirls/spools/files/flashdrive flashdrive @swirls/spools/email/resend resend @swirls/spools/vault/aes aes @swirls/spools/vault/cipherstash cipherstash @swirls/spools/agents/swirls swirls Adapters lists the packages and variables each needs. Writing an adapter @swirls/spools/adapter has the ports, types, and helpers an adapter is made from. Write your own has worked examples. Port Provides Adapter type Auth The people on the team and the accounts they sign in with AuthAdapter Store Reading and writing tables StoreAdapter FileStore Folders, files, uploads, and downloads FilesAdapter Email Sending, and reports of delivery EmailAdapter Vault Sealing and opening tokens VaultAdapter Agents Running workflows and the assistant AgentsAdapter Pages and endpoints Each route file in src/routes mounts one of these: Import What it is @swirls/spools/pages/* Route options for each page: home, list, record, tasks, notes, files, reports, workflows, integrations, assistant, sign-in, unsubscribe, and the layout around them @swirls/spools/api/* Handlers for each endpoint under /api @swirls/spools/ui/* The interface's own components, for pages you write The spools command Run in a Spool's folder. The scripts in package.json call it for you. Command What it does spools gen Checks crm.config.json and regenerates the schemas made from it spools init First run: names the CRM, sets who may use it, writes.env with fresh secrets spools harden Takes Supabase's Data API roles off the tables spools stats Recomputes the last activity, last contact, and next task dates on every record spools check-client Fails if Effect, which server code runs on, reached the browser bundle
